articles.title: Tulane vs Charlotte: Green Wave Rally to Win 38-31 in Overtime
articles.matchup: Final: Tulane (4-4) 38, Charlotte (1-7) 31 (OT), Fri., Oct. 30, Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte. Next: vs. Tulsa (Homecoming), Sat., Nov. 7, 12:00 PM ET, Yulman Stadium, New Orleans
articles.text:
Tulane 38, Charlotte 31, in overtime. Back Uptown on Friday night, the Lavin-Bernick Center set up a free Halloween-eve horror movie night in the Rat. Fine idea, but the scariest show of the night was on ESPN2, live from Jerry Richardson Stadium, and this one had a happy ending for the Green Wave.

Let me be honest about the first three acts, because we have watched enough film to know a rough plot when we see one. Charlotte led 24-14 at halftime. Conner Harrell threw two touchdowns before the break, Henry Rutledge ran 22 times for 121 yards, and the 49ers held the ball for 33:47 without a single turnover. When Derrick Eley punched in a 1-yard run with 10:52 left, it was 31-21, and I was ready to hide behind the couch.

Then Trace Johnson grew up in about 11 minutes. He finished 28 of 36 for 284 yards, and he was surgical when it mattered. Johnnie Daniels ran 13 times for 99 yards and two scores, and Cooper Helmke's 27-yard field goal made it a one-score game. Up 31-24 with 1:52 left, Charlotte went for it on fourth down at our 42. Garrett Mmahat knocked the ball loose, it squirted out of bounds short of the sticks, and we had it back.

What came next goes in the scrapbook. Daniels ripped off 33 yards up the middle on third down, Johnson ran for a first down at the 11, and with 10 seconds left he found Cameron Roberts in the end zone. Helmke's kick tied it at 31-31.

In overtime, Destyn Hill caught two throws to set it up, and Dagan Bruno plowed in from a yard out. Then Charlotte got first-and-goal at our 4, and the defense stood up four straight times. TJ Smith broke up one throw to Jaden Barnes, and E'zaiah Shine knocked away the last one. Game over.

TJ Smith also returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown in the second quarter, the kind of play kids will dress up as next Halloween. Dickson Agu made 14 tackles, and Kevin Adams III added 10.

We are 4-4 and 2-2 in the American, and after last week's loss to UTSA at Yulman, this bounce-back felt like a second wind off the river. Homecoming is next, with Tulsa coming to Yulman Stadium on Nov. 7. Roll Wave.

articles.title: Sacramento State vs Kent State: Hornets Grab First MAC Win 31-10
articles.matchup: Final: Sacramento State (2-7) 31, Kent State (3-6) 10, Fri., Oct. 30, Hornet Stadium, Sacramento. Next: vs. Toledo, Wed., Nov. 4, Hornet Stadium, Sacramento
articles.text:
Sacramento State 31, Kent State 10. Friday was Healthcare Appreciation and AANHPI Heritage Night at Hornet Stadium, and the postgame fireworks came back. This time they went up over the first Mid-American Conference win in program history, in front of 9,931 fans. Plate it up, chef. This one goes in the cookbook.

Kent State hit us early. Dru DeShields escaped trouble in his own end zone and found Wayne Harris for 92 yards, and the Golden Flashes led 7-0 in the first quarter. Grant Meadors kept us close with field goals from 42 and 28 yards, but Kent State kicked one at the horn, and we went in down 10-6. Back to the kitchen? Not this time.

The second half was 25-0, all Hornets, and the defense ran the kitchen. Five takeaways, our most since five at Incarnate Word on Sept. 7, 2017. Fata Puloka forced two fumbles and Xavier Williams forced another on a sack. Miles Bailey recovered two, and Boogsie Silvera recovered one to go with a game-high 10 tackles. On third-and-5 in the fourth quarter, Donovan Turner jumped a throw and ran it back 38 yards for a touchdown, his first trip to the end zone since his senior year at Long Beach Poly in 2021. Malikai Nichols added an interception in the end zone in the final two minutes.

Isaiah Ene carried the main course. He ran 19 times for a career-high 107 yards and two touchdowns. His 35-yard run late in the third put us ahead to stay, and he ran in the two-point try himself to make it 17-10. His 5-yard run with 2:55 left closed it out. Meadors went 3 of 3 on field goals, adding a 36-yarder, and Hamish Adams averaged 45.3 yards on six punts. We ran for 161 yards on 42 carries, and Jackson Sharman went 14 of 25 for 117 yards with no interceptions.

Kitchen cleanup: 10 penalties for 89 yards, and Kent State outgained us 302 to 278. We will sharpen the knives on that. But this win tastes like the first plate off a brand-new menu.

We're 2-7 and 1-5 in the MAC. Toledo comes to Hornet Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 4, for Senior Night. Fire up the grill. Go Hornets!

articles.title: Kent State vs Sacramento State: Five Turnovers Sink Flashes 31-10
articles.matchup: Final: Sacramento State (2-7) 31, Kent State (3-6) 10, Fri., Oct. 30, Hornet Stadium, Sacramento. Next: at Bowling Green, Tue., Nov. 10, Doyt L. Perry Stadium, Bowling Green
articles.text:
Sacramento State 31, Kent State 10. Back home on Friday, families trick-or-treated through downtown Kent from Hometown Bank Plaza, and the Kent Student Center handed out candy all afternoon. Hours later, out at Hornet Stadium in Sacramento, our Golden Flashes kept the Halloween spirit going the wrong way. We handed out the treats. Five turnovers. Five.

It started like a Halloween miracle. The Hornets fumbled on their second snap and Josue Cordoba fell on it at their 24, though we came away empty. Then, backed up at our own 8, Dru DeShields got flushed into his own end zone, kept his eyes downfield and found Wayne Harris near midfield. Harris did the rest, 92 yards, the longest Kent State touchdown this season, and we led 7-0. Harris finished with three catches for 122 yards.

Tommy Newcomb drilled a 29-yard field goal as the first half ended, and we went in up 10-6. I said nothing good lasts. I hate being right. The second half went 25-0 the other way. Brandon White had already lost a fumble late in the first half, and DeShields lost two more after the break. On third-and-5 in the fourth quarter, Donovan Turner jumped a throw and ran it back 38 yards for a touchdown. Nolan Good's late throw from their 6 was intercepted in the end zone. Isaiah Ene ran 19 times for 107 yards and two scores, and Grant Meadors went 3 of 3 on field goals.

Honest film session: DeShields went 16 of 33 for 190 yards with one touchdown and one interception, and he ran 10 times for 43 yards. We were 4 of 13 on third down, 1 of 3 on fourth down, and we ran for 93 yards. The defense did its job for long stretches. Trey Rubinstein and Antonio Bottiggi each had a sack, and Josue Cordoba and Hayden Dawahare made six tackles apiece. We outgained them 302 to 278 and still lost by 21. It is the football, folks. Hold on to it.

I went to a school with a famous fashion program, so I grade the uniforms every week. The uniforms were fine. The ball security needs a full redesign.

We are 3-6, 2-3 in the MAC and 0-5 on the road. Next is Bowling Green at Doyt L. Perry Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 10. I expect the worst. I would love to be wrong. Go Flashes.

articles.title: Carolina Panthers vs Green Bay Packers Week 8: Panthers Fall 27-19
articles.matchup: Final: Carolina Panthers (3-4) 19, Green Bay Packers (5-3) 27, Thu., Oct. 29, Lambeau Field, Green Bay. Next: vs. Denver Broncos, Sun., Nov. 8, 1:00 PM ET, Bank of America Stadium, Charlotte
articles.text:
Green Bay Packers 27, Carolina Panthers 19. Charlotte opened a packed Halloween sports weekend with Carolina Panthers vs Green Bay Packers in Week 8, and the Queen City still has the 49ers on Friday and Charlotte FC's Fan Appreciation finale on Saturday at Bank of America Stadium. We needed a treat from Lambeau Field. We got a trick, and the Panthers dropped to 3-4. Somehow we are still first in the NFC South.

It started like a dream. Rookie linebacker Jackson Kuwatch forced a fumble on the opening kickoff, and Nick Hampton recovered it. Ryan Fitzgerald soon hit a 39-yard field goal. Chuba Hubbard punched in a 1-yard run early in the second quarter for a 10-6 lead, and then Nick Scott forced another fumble that Bobby Okereke fell on. Then rookie safety Zakee Wheatley intercepted Jordan Love at the Carolina 2 in the fourth quarter. Three takeaways on the road. That is supposed to win you a game.

We turned those three takeaways into three points. That is the whole story in one sentence.

Bryce Young got sacked six times and finished 23 of 41 for 209 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Our offense went 5 of 18 on third down and gained 258 yards. Hubbard was the one thing working all night, with 81 yards on 22 carries plus seven catches for 38. Tetairoa McMillan caught six balls for 58 yards. Jalen Coker caught a fourth-and-3 throw and broke it for a 26-yard touchdown with 5:37 left to make it 27-19. The two-point try got tipped, and a fourth-and-5 at midfield came up short with 2:41 to go.

The secondary deserves a medal just for finishing. Rookie cornerback Will Lee III was carted off with a hamstring injury in the second quarter, and the team finished with three healthy corners. Green Bay found holes, and Love went 30 of 41. Fitzgerald also drilled a 50-yarder. Sam Martin averaged 48.8 yards a punt.

So we fly home from Wisconsin, catch some soccer and some Hornets, and get ready for Denver at Bank of America Stadium on Nov. 8. First place is still ours. Go take it back.

articles.title: Green Bay Packers vs Carolina Panthers Week 8: Packers Win 27-19
articles.matchup: Final: Carolina Panthers (3-4) 19, Green Bay Packers (5-3) 27, Thu., Oct. 29, Lambeau Field, Green Bay. Next: at New England Patriots, Sun., Nov. 8, 4:25 PM ET, Gillette Stadium, Foxborough
articles.text:
Green Bay Packers 27, Carolina Panthers 19. Green Bay Packers vs Carolina Panthers in Week 8 had a pregame act nobody could top. The Milwaukee Brewers came to Lambeau Field one night after winning the first World Series in franchise history, wearing cheeseheads that read 2026 WS Champions, and one of them even took a Lambeau Leap. Wisconsin had two celebrations going in one stadium, and the Packers made sure the night ended with a win.

Jordan Love was the reason. He went 30 of 41 for 288 yards and three touchdowns, and he was not sacked once. He threw scores to three different guys: Tucker Kraft from 12 yards, Matthew Golden from 24 yards with 1:46 left in the half, and Josh Jacobs from 4 yards in the third quarter to make it 27-10. Golden finished with seven catches for 79 yards. Kraft added six for 53.

Then there is Christian Watson. He caught a 53-yarder, landed on the ball and was taken to a local hospital for tests. He came back in the second half to a roar from the tunnel and finished with eight catches for 113 yards. Lambeau has seen plenty of comebacks. That one belongs on the wall.

The defense was the real headline. Six different Packers each got a sack: Ty'Ron Hopper, Lukas Van Ness, Barryn Sorrell, Dani Dennis-Sutton, Brenton Cox Jr. and Devonte Wyatt. On top of that, Hopper batted a throw to himself for our only interception, and that set up the touchdown for a 20-10 halftime lead. To open the second half, Chris McClellan stuffed Chuba Hubbard on fourth-and-2 at midfield. Late in the game, the defense got another fourth-down stop with 2:41 left. That makes five straight opponents held to 20 points or fewer.

Now the honest part, because cheeseheads do not lie. We fumbled the opening kickoff, missed an extra point, threw an interception in the end zone up 27-13 and ran for next to nothing. Jacobs scored on a 1-yard run but finished with 39 yards on 21 carries. We went 9 of 16 on third down and 3 for 3 in the red zone, so the finishing was there. The ground game was not.

articles.title: James Madison vs Troy: Dukes Fall 24-21 in Overtime at Home
articles.matchup: Final: Troy (4-4) 24, James Madison (7-2) 21 (OT), Thu., Oct. 29, Bridgeforth Stadium, Harrisonburg. Next: at Southern Miss, Thu., Nov. 5, 8:00 PM ET, M. M. Roberts Stadium, Hattiesburg
articles.text:
Troy 24, James Madison 21, in overtime. James Madison vs Troy was our Brighten the Lights of Madison game, a white out named for a lyric from our own fight song, with white pompoms waiting on the general admission seats at Bridgeforth Stadium. For one half the lights were blinding. Then the Trojans flipped the switch, and the Dukes lost at home for the first time in 12 games.

The first half was everything we came for. Camden Coleman found Corey Scott for a 2-yard touchdown, then hit Braeden Wisloski for 31 more, and it was 14-0 after one quarter. Seth Cromwell finished a third straight scoring drive with a 14-yard run, and we went to the locker room up 21-7. Cromwell ended with 135 yards on 23 carries, his first 100-yard game as a Duke, and he earned every inch of it.

Then came the part I would rather skip, but a real fan reads the whole box score. We turned it over five times, three interceptions and two lost fumbles, and drew 10 flags for 71 yards. The second play of the second half was an interception that Justin Powe returned 37 yards for a touchdown. A strip later set up Troy's tying run. After that 21-7 halftime lead, we did not score again for the final 38:41.

The defense deserves better than this headline. Amar Thomas had two sacks and six tackles. Nakian Jackson, TJ McGill and Rasheed Lovelace each made seven stops. Troy went 0 for 3 on fourth down and missed a 49-yarder late in regulation. Coleman finished 14 of 25 for 175 yards and two touchdowns, and Michael Scott caught four balls for 68 yards. We outgained them 408 yards to 349. That should win at home. Not with five giveaways.

Overtime hurt the most. We got one first down, then got stopped on fourth-and-1 from the 5, and Troy kicked a 27-yarder to end it. That is two straight overtime losses, and the 11-game home streak is gone.

Here is the good news. We are 7-2, 4-2 in the Sun Belt and still first in the East. We go to Southern Miss on Thursday, Nov. 5, for another night game. Pack the white jerseys away for now. Start wearing purple again.

articles.title: Troy vs James Madison: Trojans Stun Dukes 24-21 in Overtime
articles.matchup: Final: Troy (4-4) 24, James Madison (7-2) 21 (OT), Thu., Oct. 29, Bridgeforth Stadium, Harrisonburg. Next: vs. Louisiana Tech, Sat., Nov. 7, 4:00 PM ET, Veterans Memorial Stadium, Troy
articles.text:
Troy 24, James Madison 21, in overtime. On Tuesday night, TROYAPALOOZA brought the Janice Hawkins Cultural Arts Park a costume contest, a concert and fried Oreos. Two nights later, Troy vs James Madison gave us the best costume change of the week. The Trojans walked into Bridgeforth Stadium dressed as a team down 21-7 at halftime and walked out as the team that ended the Dukes' 11-game home winning streak.

Let me introduce Justin Powe to the rest of the country. He intercepted three throws, which ties Ronnie Shelley's single-game school record from 1968. The biggest came on the second play of the second half, when he took it back 37 yards for a touchdown. Just like that it was 21-14, and you could feel the whole stadium tighten up.

Then the defense took over. After the Dukes scored on their first three drives, they did not score again for the final 38:41. Troy forced five turnovers. Keno Jones made 13 tackles, recovered a fumble and, in overtime, stuffed Seth Cromwell on fourth-and-1 from the 5. Donnie Smith got his seventh sack of the season. That is how you avenge last year's Sun Belt Championship Game on the other team's own field.

On offense, we pounded the ground the way Troy football should. We ran it 45 times for 170 yards. Jaheim Merriweather broke a 28-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to tie it at 21-21, and he finished with 84 yards on 13 carries. Gavin Griffin opened our scoring with a 1-yard run on the first play of the second quarter, then gained 8 yards on third-and-6 in overtime to set up the kick. Tucker Kilcrease made his first start of the season and went 15 of 31 for 179 yards without an interception.

I will be fair to my own team. We went 0 for 3 on fourth down, and Hayden Wolfe missed from 49 yards late in regulation. But the kid came back in overtime and put a 27-yarder straight down the middle. It was his first field goal at Troy and our first walk-off kick in the final minute or overtime since 2020. Evan Crenshaw also averaged 45.6 yards on five punts.

We are 4-4 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt, and The Vet gets Homecoming against Louisiana Tech on Nov. 7. Save me a fried Oreo.

articles.title: Florida Atlantic vs North Texas: Owls Fall 48-41 as Messer and Veltkamp Set Records
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Atlantic (5-3) 41, North Texas (6-2) 48, Thu., Oct. 29, DATCU Stadium, Denton. Next: vs. UTSA, Thu., Nov. 5, 7:30 PM ET, Flagler Credit Union Stadium, Boca Raton
articles.text:
North Texas 48, Florida Atlantic 41. Florida Atlantic vs North Texas was our first game on ESPN since the 2020 Montgomery Bowl, and the Owls flew into Denton five days after the Rice shootout like they owned the whole sky. We did not get the win. We did get a night the record book will remember, and Boca Raton is not handing the sky back.

Easton Messer caught 16 balls for 189 yards and three touchdowns. Sixteen catches is the program record and tied for the most by any FBS player this season, and the man caught every throw that came his way. His 12-yard grab on fourth-and-4 with 39 seconds left in the half, slipping between two defenders, tied it 24-24. His 34-yarder with 8:26 to go pulled us within three. On our campus the burrowing owls dig in and refuse to move, and Messer played like one of them all night.

Caden Veltkamp went 37 of 56 for 452 yards and five touchdown throws, which ties the program record he has now matched three times. He also became the first Owl quarterback with more than one 400-yard game. Dominique Henry caught 10 balls for 116 yards, a career high, and Kaden Shields-Dutton touched it four times for 53 yards on one drive and finished it on a 22-yard shovel throw for a touchdown. Collin Rogers hit both field goals, including a 43-yarder with 1:56 left.

Here is the honest film session. Two turnovers flipped it. A third-quarter strip-sack set up the North Texas score that made it 34-24, and an interception near their goal in the fourth quarter cost us points we badly needed. The defense allowed 644 yards and 31 first downs, and North Texas held the ball for 35:05. Jahiem White ran for 193 yards. Joseph Sipp Jr. made eight tackles trying to plug it all by himself. When the onside kick bounced the wrong way, the clock did the rest.

We still went 10 of 18 on third down and 2 of 4 on fourth down, on the road, against the top team in the American. That is not a team that folds.

Now the Owls come home at 5-3. UTSA visits Flagler Credit Union Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 5, for Paradise Appreciation and Vice Night, our first Thursday home game since 2006 and the first ever at Flagler Credit Union Stadium. Bring the noise. Messer will bring the hands.

articles.title: North Texas vs Florida Atlantic: Mean Green Survive 48-41 Shootout
articles.matchup: Final: Florida Atlantic (5-3) 41, North Texas (6-2) 48, Thu., Oct. 29, DATCU Stadium, Denton. Next: vs. Rice, Sat., Nov. 7, 4:00 PM ET, DATCU Stadium, Denton
articles.text:
North Texas 48, Florida Atlantic 41. Five days after Denton's Day of the Dead Festival sent coffins racing downtown and lanterns glowing through the Twilight Lantern and Costume Parade, North Texas vs Florida Atlantic turned DATCU Stadium into its own haunted house on a wet Thursday night. The Owls kept rising from the grave. The Mean Green kept burying them anyway, and now we are 6-2, 4-0 in the American and bowl eligible for a third straight season.

Start with the quarterback, because Tayven Jackson earned the first paragraph and then some. He went 33 of 46 for 404 yards, four touchdown throws and zero interceptions, then ran five times for 41 more. That is not a game manager. That is a conductor. Our offense piled up 644 yards and 31 first downs, went 8 of 14 on third down and held the ball for 35:05. The Owls' offense spent a lot of the night watching from the bench.

Jahiem White ran 26 times for 193 yards and two scores, and his 59-yard sprint late in the second quarter put us back in front, 24-17. Justin Stevenson caught nine balls for 119 yards and a score. Kyle Koch matched him with nine grabs, went for 78 yards and scored twice, including the 2-yard dagger with 4:02 left that made it 48-38. Max Reese added seven catches for 85 yards, and Dalton Carnes turned three catches into 66.

Now the honest part, because a real fan does not hide the film. White put the ball on the turf twice, and Florida Atlantic recovered both. Easton Messer caught 16 balls for 189 yards and three touchdowns, and he caught every throw sent his way. Caden Veltkamp threw for 452 yards. Our secondary spent the night chasing a receiver who apparently cannot be tackled by rain, by brackets or by prayer, though I tried that last one.

But the defense made the two plays that decided it. Brayden Knox stripped Veltkamp on a sack in the third quarter, and we turned that into a 34-24 cushion. Peyton Taylor then intercepted Veltkamp near our goal in the fourth quarter and added seven tackles. Curlee Thomas IV got home for a sack too. Dominic De Freitas went 2 for 2 on field goals, including a 48-yarder, and the late onside kick did not go Florida Atlantic's way.

Five straight wins. A 4-0 league start for the first time since 2004, when we played in the Sun Belt. Rice comes to Denton for Homecoming on Nov. 7, and the coffins can stay in the garage. We are not done yet.

articles.title: New Mexico State vs Jacksonville State: Aggies Shut Out 24-0 at Home
articles.matchup: Final: Jacksonville State (6-2) 24, New Mexico State (3-5) 0, Wed., Oct. 28, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces. Next: vs. Liberty, Sat., Nov. 7, 8:00 PM ET, Aggie Memorial Stadium, Las Cruces
articles.text:
Jacksonville State 24, New Mexico State 0. The Organ Mountains were going dark above Las Cruces on the Wednesday before Halloween, and the scariest sight in town was the zero next to our name at Aggie Memorial Stadium. A home shutout is a trick nobody in Dona Ana County asked for.

Let me start with the good, because there was some. James Jones ran 20 times for 112 yards, and TJ Washington Jr. added 70 on 10 carries. We ran for 192 yards at 5.6 a carry, and on the ground we could hang with anybody. Our defense kept it 7-0 at halftime, too.

Tory Gethers was everywhere, with 10 tackles and two for loss. RJ Chapman intercepted Caden Creel and brought it back 53 yards, and Josiah Charles grabbed a second interception. Brad Vislisel got home for a sack. Those guys played their hearts out.

Then the air attack never left the hangar. Adam Damante completed six of 19 throws for 29 yards with an interception. Our two field goal tries came up empty, we went 0 for 2 on fourth down, and you cannot win a game when the scoreboard never hears from you.

And then there was Creel. The Jacksonville State quarterback ran 21 times for 211 yards, including an 84-yarder, and had a hand in two of the Gamecocks' three touchdowns. Their offense ran for 324 yards and kept the ball for 35:18. When a quarterback runs like that, a defense gets tired, and ours did.

Folks around here put green chile on everything to make it better. I would put it on this film if I thought it would help.

Liberty Comes to Las Cruces

So we are 3-5 and 2-2 in Conference USA, with four games left to set this right. After an open week, the Aggies stay home at Aggie Memorial Stadium to face Liberty on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 8:00 p.m. ET. Bring a jacket, bring your voice, and please, Aggies, bring some points.

articles.title: Kennesaw State vs Middle Tennessee: Owls Snap Skid With 44-28 Win
articles.matchup: Final: Kennesaw State (2-6) 44, Middle Tennessee (4-4) 28, Wed., Oct. 28, Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro. Next: vs. Delaware, Sat., Nov. 7, 3:00 PM ET, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw
articles.text:
Kennesaw State 44, Middle Tennessee 28, and the Owls finally have a reason to hoot again. Back home, the General sits in the Southern Museum, the old locomotive taken from Big Shanty, the original name of our town, to kick off the Great Locomotive Chase. On Wednesday night in Murfreesboro, our Owls went on a chase of their own and ran down a six-game losing streak.

Rickie Collins was close to perfect. He completed 16 of 19 throws for 206 yards and three touchdowns. Dylan Gary caught only two balls, and both went for scores, from 31 and 28 yards out. Davis Bryson grabbed five for 46 yards, including a 23-yard touchdown, and he added 71 yards on kickoff returns.

Boogie Woods III opened the scoring with a 12-yard touchdown run and closed our touchdown parade with a 2-yard plunge with 5:15 left that made it 41-20. He ran 12 times for 67 yards, and he even caught the two-point conversion after the play that flipped this whole night.

That play belongs to Tywon Christopher. Early in the third quarter, with us clinging to a 19-17 lead, he jumped in front of a Roman Gagliano throw and took it 59 yards to the house. That made it 27-17, and the Blue Raiders never got closer than seven again. Isaac Paul added an interception of his own and brought it back 41 yards. Ugonna Nwoha had two sacks, and Tay'vion Lawson and Baron Hopson made nine tackles apiece.

Now, my mama raised me to tell the truth. Middle Tennessee held the ball for 40:19 and went 11 of 20 on third down. Antonio Martin ran for 106 yards. We trailed 14-7 in the second quarter, got flagged nine times for 72 yards, missed an extra point and gave up a 100-yard kickoff return late. Every one of those made me grab my hat.

Daniel Kinney bounced back from that missed kick with a 44-yard field goal with 1:55 left to make it 44-20, and Brayden Munroe ripped off 61 yards on two punt returns. When the Owls make more big plays than mistakes, the Owls win.

Delaware Comes to Kennesaw

We are 2-6 and 1-3 in Conference USA, and that first league win tastes as sweet as Sunday pie after church. After an open week, the Owls come home to face Delaware on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3:00 p.m. ET at Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium. Hoot hoot, y'all.

articles.title: Middle Tennessee vs Kennesaw State: Blue Raiders Fall 44-28 at Home
articles.matchup: Final: Kennesaw State (2-6) 44, Middle Tennessee (4-4) 28, Wed., Oct. 28, Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro. Next: vs. Western Kentucky, Sat., Nov. 7, 3:30 PM ET, Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro
articles.text:
Kennesaw State 44, Middle Tennessee 28. Murfreesboro sits at the geographic center of Tennessee, and a stone obelisk off Old Lascassas Road, about a mile from campus, marks the spot. On Wednesday night, the center of my heart took a beating in our own house, and it was our first home loss of the season.

Here is what hurts. We did almost everything you want on paper. We had 22 first downs to their 14. We outgained the Owls 380 to 318, ran for 197 yards and held the ball for 40:19. Our offense went 11 of 20 on third down. If you only read the box score, you would guess we won going away.

Antonio Martin was a workhorse, 18 carries for 106 yards, and his 7-yard touchdown run put us up 14-7 early in the second quarter. Roman Gagliano scored on a 1-yard keeper in the first quarter and ran 15 times for 47 yards. Cam'ron Lacy caught four balls for 73 yards, including a 41-yarder, and Terrence Brown had six catches.

Then came the plays that broke my heart. Dominic Bourgeois drilled a 45-yard field goal with two seconds left in the half to pull us within 19-17. But early in the third quarter, Tywon Christopher jumped a Gagliano throw and returned it 59 yards for a touchdown, and the Owls added a two-point conversion for a 27-17 lead. Gagliano finished 21 of 43 for 183 yards with two interceptions, while Rickie Collins went 16 of 19 for 206 yards and three scores on the other side.

Our defense battled. Bryce Williams made nine tackles, and Korey Smith had seven tackles, an interception and a fumble recovery. Bourgeois added a 38-yarder to make it 27-20 late in the third. Then Collins found Dylan Gary for a 28-yard score, and Boogie Woods III ran one in from 2 yards out to make it 41-20.

Santana Fleming gave us something to cheer late, taking a kickoff 100 yards for a touchdown with 1:42 left, and Gagliano ran in the two-point try. Ashton Logan averaged 47.2 yards on five punts. I will take every bit of good I can find tonight.

Rivalry Week in Murfreesboro

So we are 4-4 and 2-2 in Conference USA, and our two-game winning streak has ended. After an open week, the Blue Raiders stay home in Murfreesboro to face Western Kentucky on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3:30 p.m. ET. Rivalry week cures a lot of heartache. True Blue, always.

articles.title: Sam Houston vs Missouri State: Bearkats Fall 24-3 in Springfield
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri State (3-5) 24, Sam Houston (1-7) 3, Tue., Oct. 27, Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield, Mo.. Next: at Jacksonville State, Sat., Nov. 7, 7:00 PM ET, AmFirst Stadium, Jacksonville, Ala.
articles.text:
Missouri State 24, Sam Houston 3. Back home in Huntsville, the big statue of General Sam Houston stands 67 feet tall off the interstate, and on Tuesday night in Springfield I could have used a little of that height and a lot of that patience.

Here is the part that should not get lost. For three quarters this was a fistfight. Sam Carpenter drilled a 33-yard field goal with 31 seconds left in the first quarter, and our defense held the Bears to a single field goal the rest of the first half. It was 10-3 heading into the fourth. Josh Alexander-Felton played like a man who had heard every bad thing anybody ever said about this season. Seven tackles, two sacks and three tackles for loss. Brian Bates Jr. added seven tackles of his own.

And Cal Joseph, bless his right leg. Five punts, a 50.2 average, a 70-yard boomer, and two pinned inside the 20. When your punter is one of the best players on the field, you know it was a long night, but that young man earned his supper.

DJ Bailey kept slinging it, too. He went 20 of 35 for 258 yards with no interceptions. Grady O'Neill caught six balls for 74 yards, Chris Reed had four for 64, and Tim Burns Jr. hauled in a 46-yarder.

Now the hard part. We ran 25 times for 26 yards. You cannot live on that. We were flagged 10 times for 84 yards, we went 0 for 2 on fourth down, and the fourth quarter got away fast. Henry Belin IV hit Jmariyae Robinson for a 37-yard touchdown on the first play of the fourth to make it 17-3, a fumbled punt return set up Connor Lair's 1-yard run with 3:44 left, and our last chance ended on a fourth-down throw that got knocked away with 1:08 to go.

So we are 1-7 and 0-4 in Conference USA, and I am not going anywhere. Neither is the statue. The Bearkats get an open week, then go to Jacksonville State on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 7:00 p.m. ET at AmFirst Stadium. Eat Em Up, Kats.

articles.title: Missouri State vs Sam Houston: Bears Beat the Bearkats 24-3 at Plaster Stadium
articles.matchup: Final: Missouri State (3-5) 24, Sam Houston (1-7) 3, Tue., Oct. 27, Robert W. Plaster Stadium, Springfield, Mo.. Next: at Florida International, Sat., Nov. 7, 4:00 PM ET, Pitbull Stadium, Miami.
articles.text:
Missouri State 24, Sam Houston 3. Springfield calls itself the birthplace of Route 66, and on Tuesday night the Bears took the Bearkats on a long, slow drive with no exits. It was the first conference meeting between these two programs and the first time they had played at all since 2006, and we made sure they remember the trip.

Henry Belin IV was cool as a November morning on the square. Twelve of 18, 184 yards, two touchdowns, and not a single turnover. He opened the scoring with a 32-yard strike to Isaiah Myers with 4:09 left in the first quarter. Myers came into this one off 11 catches for 242 yards at Delaware, and he picked right up where he left off with three grabs for 77 yards.

Then came Jmariyae Robinson, and I need a minute. On the first play of the fourth quarter he caught a ball across the middle, shook off a tackler not once but twice, and carried it the rest of the way for a 37-yard touchdown that made it 17-3. Robinson finished with seven catches for 102 yards. I have watched that play eleven times. I will watch it eleven more.

The defense deserves its own parade down Glenstone. Sam Houston ran 25 times for 26 yards. Twenty-six! Jared Lloyd had seven tackles, a sack and two throws broken up, and Tim Brantley Jr. got a sack of his own. The Bearkats went 0 for 2 on fourth down, and the last one, with 1:08 left, ended with our guys knocking the ball away.

The dagger came off special teams. Sam Houston fumbled a punt return, Martavis Blackmon fell on it, and Connor Lair ran it in from a yard out with 3:44 to go. Lair carried 19 times for 75 yards and wore that defense down all night. Yousef Obeid added a 34-yard field goal, and the Bears never trailed.

We are 3-5 and 2-2 in Conference USA, and this team is playing its best football right now. After an open week, the Bears head to Miami to face Florida International on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 4:00 p.m. ET. Pack the sunscreen and the maroon.

articles.title: Western Kentucky vs Delaware: Hilltoppers Fall 35-21 After a Fast Start
articles.matchup: Final: Delaware (4-4) 35, Western Kentucky (3-5) 21, Tue., Oct. 27, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green, Ky.. Next: at Middle Tennessee, Sat., Nov. 7, 3:30 PM ET, Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, Murfreesboro, Tenn.
articles.text:
Delaware 35, Western Kentucky 21. I typed that score slowly, the way you back a Corvette out of a tight garage here in Bowling Green, the only town in America where they build the things. It still hurts to look at.

And the Hilltoppers started like a brand-new engine. Brock Glenn found CC Ezirim for a 2-yard touchdown on our first drive, Zion Taylor punched in a 1-yard run, and Ajay Allen scored from five out early in the second quarter to put us up 21-14 at Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium. I was standing on my seat. My wife was asking me to sit down. Both of us were happy.

Then the scoreboard froze for us. Western Kentucky did not score again after 10:52 of the second quarter, and Delaware put up the next 21 points.

The problem had a name, and it was Nick Minicucci. He completed his first 17 throws, finished 32 of 38 for 414 yards and four touchdowns, and Sean Wilson caught nine of them for 183 yards. When a quarterback misses six times all night, a secondary feels like it's chasing a pickup down Scottsville Road.

Now let me give our guys their due, because they earned it. Glenn ran 17 times for 129 yards, including a 61-yard burst, and threw for 224 more. Ajay Allen added 73 rushing yards and a touchdown. As a team we ran for 232 yards at 6.8 a carry, and we outgained them on the ground by a mile. Moussa Barry caught four balls for 80 yards, including a 45-yarder. Jaylen Wester and Westen Ard made nine tackles apiece, Mackavelli Malotumau had two tackles for loss, and Dave Herard jumped on a Delaware fumble.

What killed us was the middle of the field and the big downs we could not finish. Two interceptions, one deep in Delaware territory to open the fourth quarter, and only 4 of 14 on third down. You do not beat a quarterback that hot by leaving points out there.

So we sit at 3-5 and 2-2 in Conference USA, and the league is still wide open. After an open week, the Hilltoppers go to Murfreesboro to face Middle Tennessee on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3:30 p.m. ET. That is a rivalry game, and I already have the red towel packed.

articles.title: Delaware vs Western Kentucky: Nick Minicucci Throws for 414 in a 35-21 Blue Hens Win
articles.matchup: Final: Delaware (4-4) 35, Western Kentucky (3-5) 21, Tue., Oct. 27, Houchens Industries-L.T. Smith Stadium, Bowling Green, Ky.. Next: at Kennesaw State, Sat., Nov. 7, 3:00 PM ET, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw, Ga.
articles.text:
Delaware 35, Western Kentucky 21, and I want it read out loud on Main Street in Newark. The Blue Hens went to Bowling Green, Kentucky, on a Tuesday night and came home with a road win, which this program had not done in seven straight trips. That road streak is finished. Nobody in my house is allowed to mention it again.

Start with Nick Minicucci, because the young man was a surgeon. He completed his first 17 throws, a Delaware record for straight completions to open a game, and finished 32 of 38 for 414 yards and four touchdowns. He also climbed to fourth in program history with 6,459 career yards. A week after he tied the school record with five touchdown throws, he went out and made more history on a weeknight.

Sean Wilson was the guy Minicucci kept looking for, and who could blame him? Nine catches. 183 yards. Touchdowns of 21 and 40 yards. That 40-yarder with 4:20 left in the third quarter made it 35-21, and nobody scored again. Kaderris Roberts caught seven balls and opened our scoring with a 17-yard touchdown, and Jo Silver grabbed an 8-yard score with 59 seconds left in the half to give us our first lead at 28-21.

Now, honesty is a family value in my house. The Hilltoppers jumped us 7-0 and 14-7, and Brock Glenn ran for 129 yards on 17 carries. Western Kentucky piled up 232 rushing yards. My blood pressure would like a word with our run defense.

But this defense found a second gear after halftime and held the Hilltoppers scoreless for the final 30 minutes. Kevin Moore picked off a throw late in the first quarter, and AJ Graham got his first career interception on the first play of the fourth, deep in our own end, which shut the door for good. Gavin Moul led us with seven tackles, and Dominick Brogna got home for a sack.

The Blue Hen is our state bird, and tonight every one of them in the First State is crowing. We are 4-4 and 2-2 in Conference USA, right back in the middle of things. After an open week, the Blue Hens head to Kennesaw State on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3:00 p.m. ET. Bring the whole flock.

articles.title: And the Crown Goes to... Indiana! Hoosiers Win at the Big House for the First Time Since 1967
articles.byline: Mallory Penhallow, The Indiana Fanatic
articles.matchup: Indiana 13, Michigan 6 (final, OT), Sat., Oct. 24, Michigan Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, America. I'd like to thank the judges, the Big House, and every single Hoosier who stood in the cold until overtime. Mallory Penhallow here, former Miss Monroe County runner-up, and darlings, I finally have a crown. Indiana 13, Michigan 6, in overtime, in front of 111,276 people. The AP says it's Indiana's first win at Michigan Stadium since 1967. Fifty-nine years! My sash is soaked in happy tears.

Now, the talent portion was not pretty. Through four quarters, Indiana had two field goals from Nico Radicic, from 22 and 34 yards. Michigan had two field goals. Michigan's last one came as time expired, after the Wolverines reached our 3 and our defense sacked Tommy Carr for a fourth time to force the kick. Tied 6-6. Into the evening gown round we went.

Overtime, first snap: Josh Hoover, who is banged up and nearly got benched, threw a 21-yard pass to Brock Schott. Then he ran it in himself from 4 yards out. Michigan got the ball back, reached our 13, and Carr's last pass hit the turf in front of Salesi Moa just outside the end zone. I screamed so loud I lost my pageant voice.

Hero: the defense, which kept Michigan out of the end zone all day and held the Wolverines to 57 rushing yards. Rolijah Hardy made nine tackles with two sacks. Amare Ferrell intercepted a pass, and Michigan lost a fumble too. Hoover gets the crown jewel for gutting it out. The goat, affectionately: our passing game, 8 of 18 for 81 yards. Nobody wins Miss Congeniality every year.

What it means: Indiana is 7-1 and 4-1 in the Big Ten and jumped from No. 6 to No. 4 in the AP poll released Oct. 25. After coming up inches short against Ohio State, the Hoosiers still have never lost two straight in Curt Cignetti's three years, per the AP. Poise, posture and a defense that won't let you breathe.

Next up: Minnesota visits Memorial Stadium in Bloomington on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS. Halloween at home. I'm going as a 1967 Hoosier, which is to say, a winner in Ann Arbor.

Thank you, thank you. Wave from the elbow, and go Hoosiers!

articles.title: Hallelujah, Pass the Biscuits: Terrence Brown Runs Wild, Bourgeois Goes 4-for-4, and the Blue Raiders Kneel It Out in Miami
articles.byline: Opal Stonebriar, The Middle Tennessee Fanatic
articles.matchup: Middle Tennessee 26, Florida International 23 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Pitbull Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hey there, sugar. Opal Stonebriar, front-row grandma of Murfreesboro, still humming the closing hymn from Tuesday night. Take a biscuit and sit down, because Middle Tennessee went to Pitbull Stadium and won 26-23, and baby, I have not sat down since.

I'm a choir director, so here's the service in three hymns.

Hymn one: the double portion. With one second left in the first half, FIU lined up a 46-yard field goal. J. Williams blocked it, but we were offside, so they tried again. Ashton Taylor blocked that one too. Same kick, blocked twice, in one second. In my church we call that a double portion.

Hymn two: the shout. FIU tied it 16-16 late in the third quarter. Four plays later, Terrence Brown went 54 yards up the middle for a touchdown, and Rutherford County felt the floor shake. Terrence finished with 158 yards on 18 carries.

Hymn three: the benediction. FIU scored with 6:06 left to make it 26-23. Our boys took the ball at our own 25 and never gave it back. Eleven plays, 71 yards, every last second. Then we knelt down twice at the FIU doorstep. We were close enough to score. We chose mercy. That's Christian football.

My heroes: Terrence, and Dominic Bourgeois, who made field goals of 51, 39, 50 and 28 yards. Four tries, four makes. When the offering plate comes by, that young man will put it through the uprights from midfield. Roman Gagliano threw for 200 yards with no turnovers, and we held the ball for 33:13. Heavy and lasting, the way Grandma likes her pound cake.

My affectionate goat is the penalty flag: nine for 57 yards, including a holding call on that last drive that gave me the vapors.

What it means: the Blue Raiders are 4-3 and 2-1 in Conference USA, right behind 3-0 Liberty and Jacksonville State. Our bus has gas in it.

Next up, Kennesaw State visits Floyd Stadium on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 7 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network. Bring a casserole and wear that true blue. I'll save you a seat on the front row, sugar. Grandma always does.

articles.title: Ay, Abuela, the Sugar Packets Blinked: FIU Rallies Back Twice, Then Watches Middle Tennessee Keep the Ball for the Last 6:06
articles.byline: Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, The Florida International Fanatic
articles.matchup: Middle Tennessee 26, Florida International 23 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Pitbull Stadium
articles.text:
¡Hola, Panther people! Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, back at the kitchen table in Sweetwater, where abuela has knocked every domino onto the floor. Middle Tennessee beat us 26-23 on Tuesday night at Pitbull Stadium. Abuela says a loss told honestly is still a story worth telling, so here it is. Then I'm eating a pastelito.

The good first. JJ Kohl threw three touchdown passes: 49 yards to Kyle McNeal, 1 yard to Kevin Schaeffer, and 21 yards to Sterling Joseph. Down 16-8 in the third, Devonte Lyons ran in the two-point try to tie it 16-16, and I knocked my cafecito over. Worth it. Devonte had 115 yards on 19 carries. He runs like he's late for Sunday dinner at abuela's, which is the fastest a human being can move.

Now the plays that hurt. At the end of the first half, our 46-yard field goal got blocked, a penalty gave us a do-over, and it got blocked again. Twice! In one second! Four plays after we tied it, Terrence Brown went 54 yards for a touchdown. And after Kohl hit Joseph to make it 26-23 with 6:06 left, we never saw the ball again. Middle Tennessee ran 11 plays and knelt down at our doorstep. Abuela says keeping the dominoes for six straight minutes is not a strategy, it's a hostage situation.

My hero is Wesley Miller. Sixteen tackles, 13 of them solo. Abuela asked if he was twins. He is just everywhere, like a cousin at a quinceañera.

My goat, with love: the field goal gremlins. Block it the third time and see what happens, abuela says.

What it means: FIU is 3-4 and 1-2 in Conference USA, with back-to-back losses by exactly three points, at Jacksonville State and now at home. Abuela says, "Mija, a team that keeps losing by three is about to start winning by three." I wrote it on a napkin.

To Opal and the Blue Raider folks: congratulations. Enjoy the biscuits. We had croquetas, and we're fine emotionally, thank you.

Next up, FIU visits 6-1 Liberty at Williams Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network. It's Halloween, so I'm dressing the sugar packets up as a brick wall. Bring a colada. ¡Vamos, Panthers!

articles.title: Rapids Ahead: Isaiah Myers Goes for 242, but the Bears Flip the Canoe in Newark
articles.byline: Clementine Bilyeu, The Missouri State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Delaware 61, Missouri State 38 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Delaware Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy from the Ozarks. Clementine Bilyeu here, wringing out my socks on the bank of the James River. I guide float trips for a living, and Tuesday night in Newark was one of those floats where the first hour is glorious and then you meet a rock with your name on it. Delaware beat us 61-38.

The glorious part was real. J.J. O'Neal grabbed a Delaware pass and took it back 47 yards for a touchdown, and we led 14-7 after one quarter. Henry Belin IV found Isaiah Myers twice for touchdowns, the second with 14 seconds left in the half, and the Bears went to the locker room up 28-24. Connor Lair ran for two touchdowns, and we were still ahead 35-31 midway through the third.

Then came the rock. Down 38-35, Belin got sacked by Jawarren Corbin, the ball came loose, and B. Gorham returned it 59 yards to our 4. Delaware scored on the next play. After that, Corbin intercepted Belin, George Mullins intercepted Belin, and Delaware rattled off 30 straight points. That's not a rapid, friends. That's a waterfall.

My hero is Isaiah Myers: 11 catches, 242 yards, two touchdowns. He was a downstream current all night, and I'd let him steer my canoe anytime. Belin threw for 337 yards and kept chucking it, God bless him.

My affectionate goat is the yellow flag: 12 penalties for 100 yards. You can't paddle upstream with the anchor dragging, kids.

What it means: the Bears are 2-5 and 1-2 in Conference USA. That's a bumpy float, but there's a lot of river left, and the next stretch is calm water at home.

Next up, Sam Houston comes to Plaster Stadium on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Plaster's been around since 1941, built as a WPA project, so it's seen worse nights than this one, and better ones coming. Pack a snack and a dry bag, Bears fans. We're putting back in.

articles.title: Overdue Notice Paid in Full: Minicucci Throws Five Touchdowns, Corbin Wrecks the Night, and the Blue Hens Drop 61
articles.byline: Hen Lofland, The Delaware Fanatic
articles.matchup: Delaware 61, Missouri State 38 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Delaware Stadium
articles.text:
Good evening, and you may raise your voices. Hen Lofland here, from behind the circulation desk in Newark, where I am officially stamping the losing streak "RETURNED." Delaware beat Missouri State 61-38 on Tuesday night, ending a three-game skid, and I have not shushed a single soul since.

Let me footnote the turning points.

Footnote one: halftime. We trailed 28-24, and Missouri State's Isaiah Myers was having the night of his life. Then Nick Minicucci came out and threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to Jo Silver and a 3-yarder to Elijah Sessoms. We were back in front 38-35.

Footnote two: the chapter break. Jawarren Corbin sacked Henry Belin IV, the ball came loose, and B. Gorham scooped it and ran 59 yards to the Missouri State 4. Minicucci ran it in himself on the next snap. Corbin wasn't finished, either. He intercepted Belin in the fourth, George Mullins had one too, and we scored 30 straight points before the Bears kicked a late field goal. That's not a comeback. That's a sequel.

Footnote three: Bryson Graves, who returned five kickoffs for 160 yards, including runbacks of 42 and 63 in the third quarter. Every time Missouri State kicked to him, I heard a page turn.

My hero is Minicucci: 20 of 29 for 225 yards, five touchdown passes, plus a rushing touchdown. Six touchdowns in one night. I'd like to have that bound and shelved. Corbin is co-hero for a sack, a forced fumble and an interception. Jo Silver ran for 101 yards, and we went 5-for-5 on fourth down.

Goat? Fine, the defense gave up 242 receiving yards to one man. We'll call that a book we checked out but did not finish.

What it means: the Blue Hens are 3-4 and 1-2 in Conference USA. Delaware claims six national titles. Tuesday felt like chapter one of a seventh, and I'm only a little biased.

Next up, Delaware visits Western Kentucky on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 7 p.m. ET on CBS Sports Network. Two Tuesdays in a row under the lights. Bring your library card and your loudest voice. Book club meets at kickoff.

articles.title: Float Stalled at the Judges' Stand: South Alabama Ties It Late, Then Watches Marshall Roll Past 20-13
articles.byline: Azalea Fairhope-Grice, The South Alabama Fanatic
articles.matchup: Marshall 20, South Alabama 13 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Joan C. Edwards Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hey, y'all. Azalea Fairhope-Grice here, beads still around my neck and glue gun unplugged in mourning. I grade football like a Mardi Gras float: Is it bold? Does it move? Did the crowd scream? Tuesday night in Huntington, our float was gorgeous for three and a half quarters, then lost a wheel in front of the judges. Marshall won 20-13.

Here's how the parade went sideways.

First, the long stall. It was 6-6 at the half on four field goals, and our offense went 4-for-18 on third down. Jared Hollins completed 12 of 33. That's a float stuck at the corner of Government and Royal while the crowd checks its watch.

Second, the one bead we threw to the wrong side of the street. In the third quarter, Cole Funderburk intercepted Hollins at midfield, Marshall hit a 38-yard pass, and Zion Turner ran it in from the 3. Then Davis Little missed a 45-yarder.

Third, the gut punch. PJ Martin, bless him, ran 19 yards for the tying touchdown with 4:38 left, and I screamed so loud a krewe captain in Mobile turned around. Marshall answered with eight plays and 75 yards, and Judah Price scored from the 5 with 1:49 to go. Our last drive ended on a fourth-down incompletion at our own 34.

My hero is PJ Martin, plus a defense that held Marshall to 328 yards while Marshall's kicker missed from 49 and 27. And we went 5-for-6 on fourth down. That's a float with guts.

My affectionate goat is third down. Four for 18, darlin'. My volleyball girls convert more than that serving underhanded.

What it means: the Jaguars are 4-3 and still 2-1 in the Sun Belt. One bad parade doesn't cancel Carnival, and Mobile invented Carnival in this country, back in 1703. We know how to come back next year. Or next week.

Next up, Louisiana Tech comes to Hancock Whitney Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home. Dress up as a first down, y'all. Throw me 20.

articles.title: We Are... Clutch: Judah Price Punches It In With 1:49 Left, and the Herd Holds On at the Joan
articles.byline: Mercy Holderby, The Marshall Fanatic
articles.matchup: Marshall 20, South Alabama 13 (final), Tue. Oct. 20, Joan C. Edwards Stadium
articles.text:
How am I? We are. Mercy Holderby here, green ribbon on the microphone and a voice that is officially out of commission after Tuesday night. Marshall beat South Alabama 20-13 at Joan C. Edwards Stadium, and the night-shift nurses on my floor will have to communicate with me by sign language until Thursday.

Let me chart the vitals.

Vital sign one: patience. It was 6-6 at the half. Jorge Diaz Nicolas hit field goals from 47 and 48 yards, and our defense kept South Alabama's offense in triage.

Vital sign two: the takeaway. In the third quarter, Cole Funderburk intercepted Jared Hollins at midfield. Soon after, Zion Turner threw a 38-yard dart to Adrian Norton, and then Turner ran it in from 3 yards out. Thirteen to six, and the Joan was rocking.

Vital sign three: the code. South Alabama tied it at 13 with 4:38 left, and my heart rate did something I'd chart as "concerning." Then the Herd went 75 yards in eight plays. Khalil Wilkins ripped off 14 yards to the 9, and Judah Price bulled in from the 5 with 1:49 left. On South Alabama's last chance, B. Ward hurried Hollins into a fourth-down incompletion. Patient stable. Discharge papers signed.

My hero is Zion Turner: 21 of 33 for 181 yards, a rushing touchdown, and zero turnovers. After six turnovers against Coastal earlier this month, a clean chart is beautiful. Funderburk and Ward are co-heroes. The defense held the Jaguars to 4-of-18 on third down.

My affectionate goat: the kicking game, which also missed from 49 and 27 yards. Jorge, honey, I love you. Next time, aim for the middle.

What it means: Marshall is 4-3 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt, and that sour taste from the Coastal loss is finally gone. We needed a win at home, and the Herd brought one.

Next up, Marshall visits Old Dominion at S.B. Ballard Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 1 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween in Norfolk. I'm going as a nurse, which is not a costume, it's a lifestyle. Herd up, friends. How are we? We are... Marshall!

articles.title: Hatch Hot in Huntsville: James Jones Runs for 178, the Defense Slams the Goal-Line Door, and the Aggies Win on the Road
articles.byline: Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, The New Mexico State Fanatic
articles.matchup: New Mexico State 30, Sam Houston 24 (final), Wed. Oct. 21, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium
articles.text:
¡Buenas noches, Aggies! Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya here, a chile farmer's daughter from Las Cruces, still fanning my mouth after Wednesday night. New Mexico State beat Sam Houston 30-24 at Bowers Stadium. Our first road win of the season, and it came roasted.

On my chile scale, here are the moments that decided it.

Josiah Charles' interception: Hatch hot. In the second quarter, we trailed 7-0 after a blocked punt was returned for a touchdown, which on my scale is a jalapeño in the eye. Then Josiah picked off Landyn Locke and ran it back 25 yards to the 1. James Jones walked in on the next play.

The third quarter: ghost-pepper hot. We trailed 17-14 after an 81-yard touchdown pass. Then Adam Damante hit AJ Williams III from 5 yards out, Kyah Francone kicked a 25-yard field goal, Kaian Roberts-Day recovered a fumble, and TJ Washington Jr. scored from the 7. Sixteen points in one quarter. Somebody get me a glass of milk.

The goal-line stand: so hot I needed a minute alone. Early in the fourth, Sam Houston drove deep into our end. Our defense held, and their fourth-down pass into the end zone fell incomplete. Then, after the Bearkats made it 30-24 with 4:00 left, our offense ran six plays and never gave the ball back. James Jones moved the chains on a 2-yard run, we took a knee in spirit, and the clock hit zero.

My hero is James Jones: 27 carries, 178 yards and a touchdown. He ran like a man carrying a sack of fresh-roasted chile to the farmers market before it sells out. AJ Williams caught two touchdown passes. Our defense held Sam Houston to 11 rushing yards. Eleven!

My affectionate goat: third down. We went 2-for-12. That's a mild salsa, mijo, and we serve hot food in this house.

What it means: the Aggies are 3-4 and 2-1 in Conference USA, tied in the loss column with Middle Tennessee and WKU behind the 3-0 teams. The green chile is in season, and so are we.

Next up, Jacksonville State comes to Aggie Memorial Stadium on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN2. The Gamecocks are 3-0 in the league. Grab your green chile stew, Aggies. It's going to be a spicy Wednesday.

articles.title: A Ballad With a Sad Third Verse: Railyn Adams Shines, Tim Burns Goes 81, but the Aggies Ride Out of Huntsville With a 30-24 Win
articles.byline: Lem Coxwell, The Sam Houston Fanatic
articles.matchup: New Mexico State 30, Sam Houston 24 (final), Wed. Oct. 21, Elliott T. Bowers Stadium
articles.text:
Evenin', folks. Pull up a stump. Lem Coxwell here, Walker County born, history teacher by trade and keeper of Texas folklore by calling. Wednesday night's tale at Bowers Stadium had a hero, a villain and a sad third verse. New Mexico State won 30-24.

Verse one is a good one. Early in the first quarter, our special teams blocked a punt and Railyn Adams scooped it into the end zone. Seven to nothing before anybody found their seat. Later, Sam Carpenter hit a 38-yard field goal, and we led 10-7.

Verse two had a lightning bolt. To open the second half, Landyn Locke threw it to Tim Burns Jr., and Tim ran 81 yards for a touchdown. We led 17-14. If General Houston had a man that fast at San Jacinto, the battle would've been over in nine minutes instead of 18.

Verse three is where the ballad turns sad. New Mexico State scored 16 straight points in the third quarter, helped by a lateral that came loose on our end. Then, early in the fourth, we drove deep into Aggie territory and came away with nothing after a fourth-down throw into the end zone fell incomplete. MJ Dowdy scored from the 1 with 4:00 left after Railyn Adams intercepted Adam Damante, but the Aggies ran out the clock.

My hero is Railyn Adams: a blocked-punt touchdown and an interception. Tim Burns Jr. had 117 receiving yards. Our defense held the Aggies to 2-of-12 on third down.

My affectionate goat is the penalty flag. Thirteen of them for 118 yards. In Sam Houston's day, a man with 13 infractions got sent to the territories. We also ran for 11 yards on 20 carries. Our run game needs a revival tent.

What it means: the Bearkats are 1-6 and 0-3 in Conference USA. That's a hard chapter. But General Houston lost a few skirmishes before San Jacinto, and Huntsville still built him a 67-foot statue.

Next up, Sam Houston visits Missouri State at Plaster Stadium on Tuesday, Oct. 27, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Both teams are looking for a better verse. Bring a lawn chair and a story, folks. I'll bring the history.

articles.title: Up the Mountain, Down Again: The Dukes' Perfect Season Slips Away in Overtime in Boone, 34-31
articles.byline: Lila Shenandoah, The James Madison Fanatic
articles.matchup: App State 34, James Madison 31 (final, OT), Thu. Oct. 22, Kidd Brewer Stadium
articles.text:
Ready? Okay... actually, give me a second. Lila Shenandoah here, pom-poms drooping, glitter going everywhere, and my voice left somewhere on the side of Howard's Knob. Thursday night at Kidd Brewer Stadium, App State beat James Madison 34-31 in overtime. The zero in our loss column is gone, y'all. I'm going to cheer anyway, because that's what cheerleaders do.

Here are the three plays that broke my heart.

Play one: the interception. It was 24-24 with just over six minutes left. Colton Phares picked off Camden Coleman and returned it 21 yards to our 14. Moments later, Henry Hasselbeck threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Luke Douglas. Thirty-one to 24, and 33,322 Mountaineer fans made a noise I'll hear in my dreams.

Play two: the comeback. Dukes don't quit, honey. Camden drove us down the field, and with three seconds left, he ran it in from 6 yards out himself. Thirty-one all! I did a toe-touch so high I may have entered North Carolina airspace.

Play three: overtime. We had the ball first, lost 11 yards on a run, and Morgan Suarez's 47-yard kick missed. Then James London kicked a 40-yarder for App State, and that was that.

My hero is Braeden Wisloski, who caught a 70-yard touchdown pass from JC Evans that had me shrieking. Camden also deserves a cartwheel: 232 passing yards, a touchdown pass and the tying score.

My affectionate goat is the kicking game. Suarez went 1-for-3 and had one blocked. Morgan, sweetie, it's okay. We still love you. We also went 2-for-15 on third down, which is not a cheer, it's a cry for help.

What it means: the Dukes are 7-1 and 4-1 in the Sun Belt. One loss, on the road, in overtime, on a mountain. That's a stumble, not a fall. Harrisonburg has the best food in Virginia, and we'll eat our feelings downtown this weekend.

Next up, Troy comes to Bridgeforth Stadium on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Home sweet home. Ready? Okay! "Purple! Reign! Shake it off and win again!"

articles.title: The View Was Worth the Climb: James London Splits It in Overtime, and App State Knocks Off Unbeaten JMU in Overtime
articles.byline: Zebulon 'Zeb' Coldiron, The App State Fanatic
articles.matchup: App State 34, James Madison 31 (final, OT), Thu. Oct. 22, Kidd Brewer Stadium
articles.text:
Mornin' from the porch. Zeb Coldiron here, notebook open, coffee long gone cold, and voice gone hoarse from Thursday night. Kidd Brewer Stadium, 33,322 strong, wind off the ridge, and a 7-0 James Madison team came up our mountain. They left with a loss. App State won 34-31 in overtime. Let's take this hike one switchback at a time.

Switchback one: the takeaway. It was 24-24 with about six minutes left when Colton Phares picked off Camden Coleman and returned it 21 yards to the JMU 14. Moments later, Henry Hasselbeck hit Luke Douglas for a 4-yard touchdown. Hasselbeck also threw the earlier touchdown pass to Chris Lofton that, with Malachi Singleton's two-point pass to Sam Pickett III, tied it at 21. Not bad for a backup.

Switchback two: the loose gravel. JMU drove the length of the field and scored with three seconds left. Thirty-one all. I said a word on the porch my mama wouldn't have approved of.

Switchback three: the summit. JMU had the ball first in overtime and lost 11 yards on a run. Their 47-yard kick missed. Then we ran two plays, set it up in the middle, and James London split it from 40.

My hero is James London. Four field goals on four tries, including the winner, plus two extra points. That's 14 points from a kicker. Malachi Singleton deserves a nod too: 26 of 40 for 271 yards and two touchdowns. And the defense blocked a field goal and held JMU to 2-of-15 on third down.

My affectionate goat: the late lead we let slip. Up seven with under six minutes left, and we gave up a tying drive. That one made my blood pressure climb faster than the road up from Blowing Rock.

What it means: App State is 5-2 and 2-1 in the Sun Belt after its second straight win, and we just beat the conference's last unbeaten team. Boone sits at 3,333 feet, and the view from up here looks mighty fine.

Next up, App State visits Georgia Southern at Allen E. Paulson Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 6:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween in Statesboro. Bring a jacket, Mountaineers. Slow down, the view's worth the wait.

My affectionate goat: the late lead we let slip. Up seven with under six minutes left, and we gave up a tying drive. That one made my blood pressure climb faster than the road up from Blowing Rock.

What it means: App State is 5-2 and 2-1 in the Sun Belt after its second straight win, and we just beat the conference's last unbeaten team. Boone sits at 3,333 feet, and the view from up here looks mighty fine.

Next up, App State visits Georgia Southern at Allen E. Paulson Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 6:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween in Statesboro. Bring a jacket, Mountaineers. Slow down, the view's worth the wait.

articles.title: Sixth Straight Blessing: Jaylon Coleman Scores Twice, the Defense Steals Two, and Liberty Rolls at Kennesaw State, 34-6
articles.byline: Gideon Fairweather, The Liberty Fanatic
articles.matchup: Liberty 34, Kennesaw State 6 (final), Thu. Oct. 22, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium
articles.text:
Well, praise the Lord and pass the program! Gideon Fairweather here, youth pastor, middle-school coach, and a man who drove home from Georgia on Thursday night humming hymns at highway speed. Liberty beat Kennesaw State 34-6 at Fifth Third Stadium. Revenge for two years of losses to the Owls, served with grace and a big ol' side of rushing yards.

Here's the sermon in three points.

Point one: the early fire. Kam Davis punched in a 1-yard touchdown run in the first quarter. Then, late in the quarter, Deshawn Purdie threw a 56-yard touchdown pass to Jaylon Coleman. Fourteen to nothing. My middle schoolers would say that's "bussin'." I would say it's righteous.

Point two: the fourth-down stands. Kennesaw State went for it on fourth down at our 23 in the first quarter, and E. Hopkins broke up the pass. Our defense also stopped Boogie Woods III for no gain on fourth down late in the third quarter. Brothers and sisters, that's how you hold the fort.

Point three: the turnovers. Early in the third quarter, Derrell Farrar intercepted Rickie Collins at the Kennesaw State 12, and Chase Reeves kicked a field goal. Later, Ashton McShane picked off another pass, and before the quarter ended, Jaylon Coleman ran it in from the 9 for his second touchdown. Twenty-four to 3, and the Flames were cooking.

My hero is Jaylon Coleman: a 56-yard touchdown catch and a 9-yard touchdown run. The run game also piled up 215 yards, and we held the ball for over 37 minutes. That's a sermon that runs long, and nobody minds.

My affectionate goat: the penalty flags. Twelve of them for 85 yards. Fellas, we talked about self-control in Bible study.

What it means: Liberty is 6-1, 3-0 in Conference USA, and tied at the top with Jacksonville State. That's six straight wins. Lynchburg has been here since 1757, and Thomas Jefferson called it "the most interesting spot in the state." He hadn't seen this defense.

Next up, FIU comes to Williams Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Bless these young men on both sidelines. Play hard, play fair, and let's see the joy on their faces.

articles.title: Bug Report: Liberty Crashes the Owls' System, 34-6, and Kennesaw State Needs a Major Patch
articles.byline: Ximena Holcombe-Reyes, The Kennesaw State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Liberty 34, Kennesaw State 6 (final), Thu. Oct. 22, Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, Owl Nation. Ximena Holcombe-Reyes here, logging in from Marietta. Today's post is a bug report, and it's a long one. Liberty beat Kennesaw State 34-6 on Thursday night at Fifth Third Stadium. I've run diagnostics, and here's the log.

Bug one: early crash. Liberty scored twice in the first quarter, including a 56-yard touchdown pass from Deshawn Purdie to Jaylon Coleman. In between, we went for it on fourth down at the Liberty 23, and the pass was broken up. Error 404: points not found.

Bug two: the turnovers. Early in the third quarter, Derrell Farrar intercepted Rickie Collins at our 12, and Liberty kicked a field goal. A few minutes later, Ashton McShane picked off Collins again, and Coleman ran in from the 9 to make it 24-3. Two interceptions, and Liberty put up 10 points in that quarter. That's a memory leak.

Bug three: the run defense. Liberty ran 41 times for 215 yards and held the ball for over 37 minutes. Our defense spent so long on the field that I started to worry about overheating.

My heroes are Daniel Kinney, who went 2-for-2 on field goals, and Landon Varnes, who came in and completed 9 of 15 passes for 111 yards. Our offense also put together a 12-play, 65-yard drive in the fourth quarter. Small features, but they shipped.

My affectionate goat: the scoreboard. Six points against a team we beat in 2024 and 2025. I'm not mad, Owls. I'm just running git blame.

What it means: Kennesaw State is 1-6 and 0-3 in Conference USA, and the losing streak is at six. That's a rough build. But this program only started playing football in 2015 and won the Conference USA title last year. We've debugged worse.

Next up, the Owls visit Middle Tennessee at Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium on Wednesday, Oct. 28, at 7 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Wear your gold, Owl Nation. Bugs happen. We patch them, and we ship again.

articles.title: Scuttled in Overtime: The Pirates Lead by 14, Tie It With 90 Seconds Left, and Still Sink in Memphis, 41-34
articles.byline: Bartholomew 'Bart' Quidley, The East Carolina Fanatic
articles.matchup: Memphis 41, East Carolina 34 (final, OT), Thu. Oct. 22, Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium
articles.text:
Ahoy, mateys. Bart Quidley here, and the purple tricorn hat is back in its box with a tear stain on the brim. I wore it to Memphis on Thursday night. For three quarters, it was the luckiest hat in Pitt County. Then Memphis beat East Carolina 41-34 in overtime, and now it's just a hat.

Here's how the ship went down.

First, the plunder. We led 16-3 at halftime. Noah Perez kicked four field goals on the night, including a 49-yarder as the first half ended, after D. Speer forced a punt-return fumble and B. Shirley recovered it. Early in the third, TJ Engleman Jr. ran it in from 4 yards out, and Mitch Griffis hit Landon Sides for two. Pirates 24, Tigers 10. I was ordering the grog.

Second, the mutiny. Marcus Stokes threw three touchdown passes and ran for two more after halftime. Memphis took a 34-27 lead with 3:31 left.

Third, the last broadside. Griffis drove us down the field and threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to Landon Sides with 1:30 left. Thirty-four all! I nearly threw the tricorn into the Mississippi. But in overtime, Memphis scored in two plays. We drove to the Memphis 4, and Ellis Ellis Jr. intercepted Griffis in the end zone. Down to Davy Jones' locker.

My hero is Landon Sides: seven catches, 130 yards, the tying touchdown and a two-point catch. Noah Perez went 4-for-4 on field goals and scored 14 points. Engleman ran for 92 yards.

My affectionate goat: the second half. We gave up 38 points after the break. Matey, that's not a defense, that's a plank.

What it means: the Pirates are 3-4 and 1-2 in the American after back-to-back losses, both on the road and both in overtime. Two heartbreakers in a row is a rough voyage, but Greenville has weathered worse storms. Dowdy-Ficklen holds 51,000, and it's time to fill it.

Next up, Temple comes to Dowdy-Ficklen Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home. Wear your best pirate costume, which in Greenville is just regular clothes. Hoist the colors, mateys. The tricorn is coming back out.

articles.title: The Comeback Blues: Marcus Stokes Scores Five Times After Halftime, and Memphis Rallies Past East Carolina in Overtime, 41-34
articles.byline: Otis Delaney-Crum, The Memphis Fanatic
articles.matchup: Memphis 41, East Carolina 34 (final, OT), Thu. Oct. 22, Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium
articles.text:
Well, good evening, Bluff City. Otis Delaney-Crum here, guitar on my knee, rib sauce on my sleeve, and a voice that cracked on the high notes Thursday night. Memphis beat East Carolina 41-34 in overtime at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium. That wasn't a football game, friends. That was a blues song with a happy ending.

Verse one: the sad part. At halftime, we trailed 16-3. Early in the third, East Carolina made it 24-10. The crowd went quiet like a juke joint at closing time.

Verse two: the comeback. Marcus Stokes picked up his guitar. First, a 59-yard touchdown pass to Jermane Hayes. Then a 20-yarder to Jemyri Davis. Philippe Laforge kicked a field goal. Then Stokes hit Davis again from 4 yards out to tie it at 27, and with 3:31 left, he ran it in from 2 himself. Tigers 34, Pirates 27. The whole stadium was keeping time.

Verse three: the encore. East Carolina tied it with 1:30 left, which hurt like a broken string. But in overtime, Stokes found Davis for 20 yards, then ran in from the 5. East Carolina drove to our 4, and Ellis Ellis Jr. intercepted Mitch Griffis in the end zone. Curtain down, house lights up.

My hero is Marcus Stokes: 29 of 43 for 320 yards, three touchdown passes and two rushing touchdowns, all after halftime. Jemyri Davis caught seven passes for 91 yards and two scores. Ellis Ellis Jr. had the game-ending interception, and Chauncey Logan Jr. had another.

My affectionate goat: the first half. Three points, a punt-return fumble and some sour notes. Even B.B. King tuned up before the show, fellas.

What it means: Memphis is 6-2 and 3-1 in the American, and the bad taste from the Tulane loss is gone. We're right behind UTSA, North Texas and Army in the race. Beale Street is a national historic landmark, and on Thursday night it heard a real Memphis comeback.

Next up, Army comes to the Liberty Bowl on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPNU. Halloween night against the Black Knights. Get there early, fire up the smoker and bring your loudest Go Tigers Go.

articles.title: A Dispatch From the Front: The Minutemen Fall at East Hartford, 35-16, and the Streak of Losses Reaches Four
articles.byline: Abner Kettleworth, The Massachusetts Fanatic
articles.matchup: UConn 35, Massachusetts 16 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, Pratt & Whitney Stadium
articles.text:
Hear ye, hear ye, patriots of the Pioneer Valley. Abner Kettleworth here, tricorn hat askew, musket-shaped umbrella drooping and tea gone cold on the hearth. I bring grim news from the Connecticut front. UConn beat UMass 35-16 on Friday night at Pratt & Whitney Stadium, and this dispatch is written in a trembling hand.

The battle unfolded in three acts.

Act one: the early skirmish. Derek Morris kicked a 24-yard field goal, and for a few glorious minutes, UMass led 3-0. I composed a victory ode. I should not have.

Act two: the ambush. Late in the second quarter, UConn struck twice in 32 seconds. First, Kalieb Osborne threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to JD Willoughby. Then Cyncir Bowers ran 70 yards for another. Twenty-one to 3 at halftime. The redcoats themselves never moved that fast.

Act three: the blocked punt. In the third quarter, UConn blocked our punt, and Shamar Porter fell on it in the end zone. Twenty-eight to 3. A rout, friends, though our boys fought on. William Watson III threw a touchdown pass to Curtis Kimmons IV, and Justin Williams-Thomas ran one in late.

My hero is Joseph Griffin Jr., who caught four passes for 77 yards, including a 41-yard grab. William Watson III also threw for 205 yards and didn't commit a turnover.

My affectionate goat: third down. We converted two of 14. Even the Minutemen at Lexington had better luck holding a position. We also ran for just 53 yards and committed 10 penalties for 100 yards.

What it means: UMass is 4-4 and 1-3 in the MAC, and the losing streak has reached four after a 4-0 start. The campaign has stalled, but Amherst is the home of Emily Dickinson, and she knew a thing or two about hope. It's "the thing with feathers," patriots. Let's find some.

Next up, Ball State comes to McGuirk Alumni Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 4. The kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. Onward, Minutemen. We regroup, we reload, and we march again.

articles.title: Fast Break, Helmets On: Osborne Scores Three Ways, Bowers Goes 70, and UConn Runs Away From UMass, 35-16
articles.byline: Jo Ferrante, The UConn Fanatic
articles.matchup: UConn 35, Massachusetts 16 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, Pratt & Whitney Stadium
articles.text:
Listen up, Husky Nation. Jo Ferrante here, still wearing my whistle from practice, still grinning from Friday night. UConn beat UMass 35-16 at Pratt & Whitney Stadium in front of 32,106 people. And if you tell me "nobody watches UConn football," I've got a stadium full of people who'd like a word.

Here's the game film.

Possession one: the two-minute flurry. Late in the second quarter, Kalieb Osborne threw a 20-yard touchdown pass to JD Willoughby. Thirty-two seconds later, Cyncir Bowers took a handoff 70 yards to the house. That's a fast break, folks. Get the stop, push the ball, finish at the rim. Twenty-one to 3 at halftime.

Possession two: the hustle play. In the third quarter, we blocked a UMass punt, and Shamar Porter scooped it up in the end zone. That's diving for a loose ball on the hardwood. Porter also caught a 5-yard touchdown pass in the first quarter. The man is everywhere.

Possession three: the dagger. Osborne ran it in from 13 yards out with 3:04 left. Thirty-five to 9. Ballgame.

My hero is Kalieb Osborne: 14 of 19 for 173 yards, two touchdown passes, a rushing touchdown and no turnovers. If my high school quarterbacks completed that many passes, I'd buy pizza for the whole team. Bowers ran for 131 yards on 15 carries. The run game piled up 265 yards.

My affectionate goat is the penalty flag. Eleven of them for 100 yards. Fellas, that's a lot of free throws for the other team. We also missed a 47-yard field goal. Coach Jo wants those back.

What it means: UConn is 4-3 with two straight wins, and the Huskies own New England bragging rights again. The stadium sits on Pratt & Whitney's old airfield, and the Huskies took flight on Friday night.

Next up, UConn visits Air Force at Falcon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on MW+. Halloween at altitude. Push the pace, protect the ball, and stop the penalties, Huskies. Let's go to work.

articles.title: Mission Accomplished at the Gun: Kloska Blocks a Punt, Hellums Scores Three Times, and Dawson Jones Drills a 50-Yarder to Beat Tulsa, 38-35
articles.byline: Capt. (Ret.) Thaddeus Rourke, The Army Fanatic
articles.matchup: Army 38, Tulsa 35 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, H. A. Chapman Stadium
articles.text:
Attention on deck. Capt. Thaddeus Rourke, retired, reporting from my recliner in a state of high alert. My laminated clipboard has a dent in it, and that dent is the exact shape of my fist. Friday night at H. A. Chapman Stadium, Army beat Tulsa 38-35 on a 50-yard field goal as time expired. Field report follows.

Phase one: the setback. Tulsa scored three straight touchdowns, including a 59-yard run by Trequan Jones, and took a 35-28 lead early in the fourth quarter. Mission in jeopardy. My coffee went cold, against regulations.

Phase two: special operations. Tulsa missed a 40-yard field goal. Then, with 3:52 left, T. Kloska blocked a Tulsa punt and recovered it at the Tulsa 13. Five plays later, Cale Hellums pushed in from the 1 on third down. Thirty-five all. Hooah!

Phase three: the final objective. Our defense forced a three-and-out. Julian Porter broke up a pass, and K. Harris-Miller and J. Bousum sacked Baylor Hayes. Army got the ball back at our 37 with 45 seconds left and moved 27 yards in seven plays. Then Dawson Jones stepped up and hit a 50-yarder as the clock struck zero. Target neutralized.

My heroes: Dawson Jones went 3-for-3 on field goals, from 51, 34 and 50 yards. In a game decided by three points, that's the whole margin. Cale Hellums ran 30 times for 121 yards and three touchdowns. Godspower Nwawuihe ran 12 times for 135 yards, including a 66-yard touchdown. Kloska gets a medal for the block.

My affectionate goat: the run defense in the third quarter. We gave up two long touchdown runs in four minutes. Soldiers, we will be running drills.

What it means: Army is 5-2 and 4-1 in the American after three straight wins. Last year, Tulsa beat us by one point at West Point. This year, we returned the favor on their field. Michie Stadium has stood since 1924, and the Corps has been settling accounts much longer than that.

Next up, Army visits Memphis at Simmons Bank Liberty Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 8 p.m. ET on ESPNU. Thank God for every man and woman who serves, and pack a jacket. Copy that, and beat Navy.
