articles.title: Dry Well at the Buzzer: Tulsa Strikes Oil With a 35-28 Lead, Then Army Caps the Gusher With a Last-Second 50-Yarder, 38-35
articles.byline: Wiley Pettibone, The Tulsa Fanatic
articles.matchup: Army 38, Tulsa 35 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, H. A. Chapman Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy from the Oil Capital of the World. Wiley Pettibone here, petroleum geology grad, and the only man in Tulsa who reads a box score like a well log. Friday night's log at Chapman Stadium starts with a gusher and ends with a dry hole. Army beat Tulsa 38-35 on a 50-yard field goal as time expired.

Let me walk you through the core samples.

Sample one: the gusher. Down 28-14 in the third quarter, we struck oil. David Wells Jr. ran in from 11 yards out. Then Trequan Jones broke a 59-yard touchdown run. Early in the fourth, Baylor Hayes hit Jimmy Calloway for 13 yards and a touchdown. Thirty-five to 28, Tulsa. I was pricing derricks.

Sample two: the pressure drop. Owen Carey missed a 40-yard field goal that would've put us up 10. Then, with 3:52 left, Army blocked our punt and recovered it at our 13. Army tied it from the 1 with 1:50 left.

Sample three: the dry hole. We went three-and-out, with a broken-up pass and a sack. Army got the ball at its 37 with 45 seconds left, moved 27 yards, and Dawson Jones made a 50-yarder at the gun.

My hero is Jimmy Calloway, who caught 10 passes for 88 yards and a touchdown. Baylor Hayes went 23 of 34 for 262 yards and two touchdowns, and Javon Ross scored twice, one rushing and one receiving. Trequan Jones ran five times for 66 yards. That's high yield per barrel.

My affectionate goat: the punt team. A blocked punt with 3:52 left is a blowout preventer that blew out. We also gave up 275 rushing yards to Army, which, to be fair, is what Army does.

What it means: Tulsa is 4-4 and 1-3 in the American after its third loss in four games. That stings, especially after we won at West Point last season. But the Golden Driller has stood 76 feet tall since 1966, and he's seen plenty of dry wells before the next gusher.

Next up, Tulsa gets a week off, then visits Tulane at Yulman Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. The kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. Wave at the Golden Driller on your way out of town. He can wait one more week for a win.

articles.title: Mission Grade: Scrubbed. Three Lost Fumbles Ground the Falcons in Laramie, 28-14
articles.byline: Lt. Col. (Ret.) Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, The Air Force Fanatic
articles.matchup: Wyoming 28, Air Force 14 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, War Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, wingmen. Lt. Col. Marissa Okonkwo-Hale, retired, reporting from the lawn chair with a thermos of coffee and a clipboard full of red ink. Before kickoff, I gave Wyoming the call sign "Summit," because War Memorial Stadium sits at 7,222 feet, the highest in FBS. On Friday night, Wyoming beat Air Force 28-14, and our offense ran out of oxygen.

Debrief, in three parts.

Part one: the launch failure. On Wyoming's second play from scrimmage, Tyler Hughes ran 68 yards for a touchdown. Then, on our first drive, Evan Medders fumbled, and Wyoming recovered at our 44.

Part two: the halftime deficit. Hughes threw touchdown passes to Jake Wilson and Samuel Harris, the second with 38 seconds left in the half. We trailed 21-6 despite moving the ball. Medders cut it to 21-14 in the third with a 5-yard touchdown pass to Grant Wayne and a two-point run of his own.

Part three: the fumbles. Early in the fourth, we drove to the Wyoming 14, and the ball came loose. Wyoming recovered. Four minutes later, we fumbled again near midfield, and Wyoming drove 49 yards for the clinching touchdown. Three lost fumbles, wingmen. In my day, losing equipment meant paperwork.

My hero is Evan Medders: 21 carries, 115 yards, a touchdown pass and a two-point run. The offense ran 63 times for 304 yards and held the ball for 37:45. Carter Cremascoli went 2-for-2 on field goals.

My affectionate goat: ball security. We outgained Wyoming 387 to 301 and lost by 14. That's a mission that reached the target, then forgot to release the payload.

What it means: Air Force is 5-2 and 3-2 in the Mountain West, two losses behind league-unbeaten New Mexico and still chasing. The streak of four straight wins is over. Colorado Springs sits at 6,035 feet, which is lower than Laramie, and I'm happy to be home.

Next up, UConn comes to Falcon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on MW+. Call sign: "Fast Break." Hold on to the football, Falcons. Call sign: correct.

articles.title: Yep. Tyler Hughes Goes 68 Yards on Play Two, the Defense Takes the Ball Three Times, and Wyoming Grounds Air Force, 28-14
articles.byline: Colter Sprague, The Wyoming Fanatic
articles.matchup: Wyoming 28, Air Force 14 (final), Fri. Oct. 23, War Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Colter Sprague. Laramie. Friday night, Wyoming beat Air Force 28-14 at War Memorial Stadium. Yep.

My editor says that's not enough. Pull up a hay bale.

Second play of the game. Tyler Hughes kept it and ran 68 yards for a touchdown. Seven-nothing, 50 seconds in. I spilled my coffee. Didn't mind.

Second, the turnovers. Air Force runs the ball like a cattle drive: slow, steady, all day. They ran 63 times for 304 yards and held it for over 37 minutes. But E. Bogar recovered two fumbles, including one early in the fourth after G. Rutherford knocked it loose at our 14. Air Force was driving to tie it. Didn't happen. Yep.

Third, the clincher. About four minutes later, J. Redfern forced another fumble, and S. Perez fell on it at midfield. We drove 49 yards in eight plays, and Markell Holman scored from the 1 with 3:04 left. Twenty-eight to 14. I said "yep" twice.

My hero is Tyler Hughes. He ran 12 times for 146 yards and a touchdown, and threw touchdown passes to Jake Wilson and Samuel Harris. Ran like an antelope crossing Highway 287. Bogar gets a nod. Two fumble recoveries.

My affectionate goat is our kicker, Erik Sandvik. Missed a 38-yarder. It happens. Air at 7,222 feet is light. Ball goes where it wants.

What it means: Wyoming is 5-3 and 4-1 in the Mountain West, one game behind New Mexico. Three straight wins. And we did it against Air Force, at the highest stadium in FBS. In 1870, Laramie put the first women in the world on a jury. This town has been doing big things quietly for a long time.

Next up, Wyoming gets a week off, then visits UNLV at Allegiant Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 10:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Late kickoff. Bring coffee.

That's about all I've got. Yep.

articles.title: Peer Review Rejected: Gael Ochoa Runs for 259 Yards and Five Touchdowns, but FAU Survives the Owl-on-Owl Shootout, 51-49
articles.byline: Odalys Chen-Moreau, The Rice Fanatic
articles.matchup: Florida Atlantic 51, Rice 49 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Flagler Credit Union Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning from the live oaks. Odalys Chen-Moreau here, bioengineering Ph.D., stats-cop badge on the lanyard, and a lab notebook that now contains the words "WHAT" and "HOW" in very large letters. Saturday in Boca Raton, Florida Atlantic beat Rice 51-49. Both teams are the Owls. Only one is the real Owls. The scoreboard disagreed with me.

Here's my lab report.

Observation one: Gael Ochoa is a statistical outlier. He ran 12 times for 259 yards and four touchdowns, from 55, 52, 74 and 69 yards. He also threw a 71-yard touchdown pass to Braylen Walker. That's 21.6 yards per carry. In a clinical trial, I'd ask for a second sample. In football, I'd just ask for more carries.

Observation two: the control group failed. FAU scored seven touchdowns, and Easton Messer was involved in five of them, including an 82-yard punt return with 3:37 left that made it 51-42. Our punt coverage has been placed on academic probation.

Observation three: the final experiment. Ochoa's touchdown pass to Walker cut it to 51-49 with 2:51 left. Our defense forced a three-and-out. We got the ball back at our 31 with two minutes left and moved to the FAU 37. Then Tommy Bauchiero's 55-yard field goal missed with 45 seconds left. Hypothesis: rejected.

My hero is Gael Ochoa, obviously. Max Mosey also ran for a 41-yard touchdown, and Tyvonn Byars added 93 rushing yards. Rice ran for 499 yards and gained 608 in all. Kyren Condoll had an interception.

My affectionate goat: the defense. We gave up 51 points and 339 passing yards to Caden Veltkamp. Peer review would call that a methods problem.

What it means: Rice is 1-7 and 0-4 in the American, and the losing streak is at seven. Two of those losses came by a combined four points, and this offense just showed it can score with anyone. JFK gave his Moon speech in Rice Stadium in 1962. We choose to do these things not because they are easy. Clearly.

Next up, Rice gets a week off, then visits North Texas at DATCU Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff and TV are still to be announced. Go Owls. The real ones.

articles.title: Easton Messer Rides Five Waves: Two Catches, Two Runs and an 82-Yard Punt Return Carry FAU Past Rice, 51-49
articles.byline: Kaia Brightwater, The Florida Atlantic Fanatic
articles.matchup: Florida Atlantic 51, Rice 49 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Flagler Credit Union Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, babe. Kaia Brightwater here, sunglasses on, salt in my hair and my heart rate still recovering from Saturday in Boca Raton. FAU beat Rice 51-49 at Flagler Credit Union Stadium. Owls versus Owls. Nine touchdowns of 30 yards or more. That wasn't a football game, babe. That was a hurricane swell.

Here are the waves that decided it.

Wave one: the comeback set. Rice hit us with touchdown runs of 55 and 52 yards and led 14-0 in the first quarter. Pure closeout. Then Caden Veltkamp found Branden Hoch for 30 yards, the defense got a safety, and Easton Messer scored twice. Twenty-three to 14. Clean surf, babe.

Wave two: the punt return. It was 44-42 with 3:37 left. Rice punted, and Easton Messer caught it and ran 82 yards for a touchdown. That's paddling into a monster wave, popping up and riding it all the way to the sand.

Wave three: the wipeout that wasn't. Rice scored to make it 51-49. We went three-and-out. Rice drove to our 37, and their 55-yard field goal missed with 45 seconds left. Then we knelt twice and paddled in.

My hero is Easton Messer, obviously. Twelve catches for 162 yards and two touchdowns, two rushing touchdowns and the punt-return touchdown. Five touchdowns, babe. Caden Veltkamp completed 29 of 37 passes for 339 yards and three touchdowns. A. Ware forced and recovered a fumble.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. Rice ran for 499 yards, and Gael Ochoa ran for 259 on 12 carries. Babe, that's a riptide. We need to talk about tackling.

What it means: FAU is 5-2 and 2-1 in the American, still in the race. Boca Raton is the birthplace of IBM's first personal computer, and our offense is running on the latest software.

Next up, FAU visits North Texas at DATCU Stadium on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. North Texas is 3-0 in the league, so this is a big swell. Wax the board. Surf's up on tempo, babe.

articles.title: Short Stack, Cold Syrup: The Broncos Rally From 17 Down to Tie Toledo, Then Fall at the Glass Bowl, 45-38
articles.byline: Corwin Dahlquist, The Western Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Toledo 45, Western Michigan 38 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Glass Bowl
articles.text:
Good morning, Broncos. Corwin Dahlquist here, at my usual Kalamazoo diner booth, with a syrup bottle, a pencil and a placemat full of arrows that go nowhere. Saturday at the Glass Bowl, Toledo beat Western Michigan 45-38. Our first MAC loss. The waitress brought me a refill without asking. She knew.

Here's how breakfast went.

The burnt first batch: Toledo jumped out to a 17-0 lead and led 31-14 at halftime. Our defense gave up 595 yards on the day. Pancakes that flat belong on the floor.

The fresh batch: to start the second half, Joshua Franklin returned the kickoff 92 yards for a touchdown. I hit the table so hard the creamer jumped. Broc Lowry ran one in from the 2. After Toledo scored, Lowry threw a 41-yard touchdown pass to Baylin Brooks. Then Dieter Kelly kicked a 23-yard field goal with 9:19 left. Thirty-eight all! A full stack with butter and blueberries!

The cold syrup: Toledo's CJ Miller ran 11 yards for a touchdown with 4:23 left. We got the ball back at our 23 with 1:46 left, but Israel Petite intercepted Lowry at our 48. Toledo knelt it out. Check, please.

My hero is Joshua Franklin, who returned a kickoff for a touchdown and recovered a fumble. Aveion Chenault caught six passes for 105 yards and a touchdown, including a 49-yarder. And the comeback from 17 down showed real guts. That sticks to your ribs.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. CJ Miller carried 33 times for 183 yards. That's a man eating the whole buffet. Lowry also threw two interceptions, and we went 3-for-12 on third down.

What it means: Western Michigan is 5-3 and 3-1 in the MAC, one game behind Ohio. Still in the hunt. Kalamazoo built the country's first outdoor pedestrian mall in 1959. This town knows how to keep walking forward.

Next up, Bowling Green comes to Waldo Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on CBSSN. Halloween brunch at home. Row the boat, Broncos. Next week, we order the full stack.

articles.title: Full Throttle in the Glass City: Richter Throws for 391, CJ Miller Carries 33 Times, and Toledo Holds Off Western Michigan, 45-38
articles.byline: Rocco Szczepanski, The Toledo Fanatic
articles.matchup: Toledo 45, Western Michigan 38 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Glass Bowl
articles.text:
Rocco Szczepanski here, reporting from the north-side garage with grease on my hands and a pierogi going cold on the workbench. Saturday at the Glass Bowl, Toledo beat Western Michigan 45-38. On my horsepower scale, that offense was 400 horsepower of four-wheel-drive fun. The defense, well, it needs new brake pads.

Here's the dyno sheet.

First gear: the fast start. John Alan Richter ran in from 4, Autavius Ison scored from 3, and Reice Griffith kicked a field goal. Seventeen to nothing. Then Richter threw touchdown passes to Daryl Barnett Jr. and Adjatay Dabbs, the second with 10 seconds left in the half. Thirty-one to 14. V-8, baby.

Engine trouble: Western Michigan returned the second-half kickoff 92 yards for a touchdown, and the Broncos tied it at 38 in the fourth. That's the check-engine light on the Anthony Wayne Trail.

Overdrive: CJ Miller carried the ball again, and again, and again. He scored from 11 yards out with 4:23 left. Then, after Western Michigan got the ball back, Israel Petite intercepted Broc Lowry at the WMU 48 with 1:30 left. Miller ran for a first down, and Richter took a knee. Engine off. Keys on the hook.

My hero is CJ Miller: 33 carries, 183 yards and the winning touchdown. That's a Jeep Wrangler with the doors off, climbing anything in its path. Richter completed 29 of 41 passes for 391 yards and three touchdowns, and Dabbs caught eight passes for 124 yards and two scores. Bryson Hammer added 107 receiving yards. Toledo gained 595 yards.

My affectionate goat: the kickoff coverage that let a 92-yard return happen right after halftime. Fellas, that's leaving the garage door open.

What it means: Toledo is 6-2 and 3-1 in the MAC, one game behind Ohio, and we beat the Broncos after they beat us by a point last year. The Glass City has built Jeeps for generations. This offense is built Toledo tough.

Next up, Toledo visits Sacramento State at Hornet Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Kickoff and TV are still to be announced. That's 400 horsepower of run game. Go Rockets.

articles.title: Bald Tires on the Wagon Wheel: Jordan Gant Runs for 162, but 15 Penalties and a Late Collapse Send Akron Home Empty, 35-20
articles.byline: Hollister 'Zip' Grubbs, The Akron Fanatic
articles.matchup: Kent State 35, Akron 20 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium
articles.text:
Greetings from the lab, Zips fans. Hollister "Zip" Grubbs here, tread-depth gauge in my pocket and a heavy heart in my chest. Saturday at Dix Stadium, Kent State beat Akron 35-20, and the Wagon Wheel stays in Kent. Legend says John R. Buchtel's wagon got stuck in the mud right where Kent State sits today. On Saturday, the Zips got stuck there too.

Here's my inspection report.

Good tread: we led for most of the day. Jordan Gant scored on runs of 6 and 5 yards, and Aidan Stire kicked a 40-yard field goal for a 17-14 lead late in the third quarter. Gant carried 28 times for 162 yards. That's premium all-season rubber.

The blowout: Kent State answered with a 52-yard catch and a 2-yard touchdown pass to retake the lead, 21-17. Early in the fourth, we had a chance to go ahead, but Norey Johnson intercepted Brayden Roggow at the Kent 15 and returned it 37 yards.

The flat: down 21-17 with about 7:40 left, we tried a fourth-down fake at our own 22 and came up short. Three plays later, Wayne Harris caught a 19-yard touchdown pass. Kent then got the ball back at our 13, and Dru DeShields ran it in. Four minutes, 14 points, and the wheels came off.

My hero is Jordan Gant. Kyan Mason also caught seven passes for 129 yards, and Stire hit a 50-yarder late. Our offense outgained Kent, 422 yards to 376, and held the ball for 34 minutes.

My affectionate goat: the penalty flag. Fifteen penalties for 165 yards. That's not a tire problem, friends, that's an alignment problem. Get it to the shop.

What it means: Akron is 1-7 and 0-4 in the MAC, with six straight losses. It's a bald season. But Akron is the Rubber Capital of the World, and it has hosted the All-American Soap Box Derby since 1936. We know a thing or two about rolling downhill and climbing back up.

Next up, Ohio comes to InfoCision Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 7 p.m. ET. Ohio is 4-0 in the MAC, so check the pressure, Zips. Check the tread, too.

articles.title: I Expected This (Honestly, I Didn't): Dru DeShields Throws Four Touchdowns, Wayne Harris Catches Three, and the Wagon Wheel Stays in Kent
articles.byline: Ozzie Brannigan, The Kent State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Kent State 35, Akron 20 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Zoeller Field at Dix Stadium
articles.text:
Hello. It's Ozzie Brannigan, on my bench near Brady's Leap. Saturday at Dix Stadium, Kent State beat Akron 35-20 and kept the Wagon Wheel. I expected this. I always expect this. That's not entirely true. After last week's 29-2 loss, I expected a blizzard of sadness. Instead, we scored 35 points. I've adjusted my scarf to an 8 out of 10.

Here's what happened, as calmly as I can manage.

First, the comeback. We trailed 7-0, 14-7 and 17-14. Each time, Dru DeShields answered. He hit Wayne Harris for a 1-yard touchdown before halftime, then for 55 yards in the third. Then Brandon White caught a 52-yard pass, and Hunter Hopperton caught a 2-yard touchdown. Twenty-one to 17, Flashes. I expected... no. I didn't.

Second, the interception. Early in the fourth, Akron was driving to take the lead. Norey Johnson intercepted Brayden Roggow at our 15 and ran it back 37 yards. I stood up. Nobody on my bench stood up. I'm usually alone on my bench.

Third, the knockout. Akron tried a fourth-down fake at its own 22 and came up short. Three plays later, DeShields hit Harris for a 19-yard touchdown. Then we got the ball right back at the Akron 13, and DeShields ran it in himself. Thirty-five to 17. That's 14 points in about two minutes. Good.

My hero is Dru DeShields: 294 passing yards, four touchdown passes, a rushing touchdown and no turnovers. Wayne Harris caught nine passes for 156 yards and three scores. We also committed only three penalties.

My affectionate goat: the run defense, which let Jordan Gant run for 162 yards. Also Tommy Newcomb's missed 32-yard field goal. I expected that one. Sorry, Tommy.

What it means: Kent State is 3-5 and 2-2 in the MAC, and we've won the Wagon Wheel two years running. Kent is called the Tree City, and this team just grew a new branch.

Next up, Kent State visits Sacramento State at Hornet Stadium on Friday, Oct. 30, at 10:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Do I think we'll win? I expected you to ask that. Here's the honest answer: I'm staying up to find out.

articles.title: Darlings, What a Finish: D'Shawntae Jones Scores With 1:41 Left, and Miami Steals One in Mount Pleasant, 28-27
articles.byline: Cordelia Van Doren, The Miami (OH) Fanatic
articles.matchup: Miami (OH) 28, Central Michigan 27 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Kelly/Shorts Stadium
articles.text:
Hello, darlings. Cordelia Van Doren here, back on my bench in Uptown Oxford, tea gone cold, red scarf wrapped twice around my neck for emotional support. Saturday at Kelly/Shorts Stadium, Miami beat Central Michigan 28-27. One point, darlings. I aged a decade, and I'm wearing it beautifully.

Here's the drama in three acts.

Act one: the plot twist. Early in the third, Justin Taylor intercepted Caleb Heavner and returned it 46 yards for a touchdown. Central Michigan led 17-14. I clutched my pearls so hard one popped off. Heavner answered with a 27-yard touchdown run. Very Cradle of Coaches of him.

Act two: the deficit. Central Michigan scored a touchdown and a field goal, and with 4:17 left, we trailed 27-21. I put my tea down. Things were serious.

Act three: the triumph. Our offense drove 75 yards in eight plays. Heavner threw a 27-yard pass to Maleek Huggins at the CMU 10. Then the Chippewas were flagged for pass interference twice in a row, and D'Shawntae Jones bulled in from the 2 with 1:41 left. Twenty-eight to 27. Then our defense held on downs, Jones picked up a first down, and we knelt. Curtain. Roses. Bows.

My hero is Maleek Huggins: seven catches for 122 yards, including the big one on the winning drive. Heavner ran for a touchdown and threw for 221 yards. Roosevelt Andrews III had a sack and a half.

My affectionate goat: interceptions. Heavner threw two, and one went the other way for a touchdown. Caleb, darling, we pass to the red jerseys. It's in the brochure.

What it means: Miami is 5-3 and 3-1 in the MAC after three straight wins, one game behind Ohio. And we've now beaten Central Michigan six straight times. Paul Brown, Woody Hayes, Bo Schembechler, Ara Parseghian and Sean McVay all came through Miami. Saturday, we saw why this place makes winners.

Next up, Buffalo comes to Yager Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 7 p.m. ET. A Tuesday night, darlings. Bring a blanket and your best red. Ta-ta, darlings. Love and Hawks.

articles.title: Tags Filled, Heart Broken: Four Sacks and an Interception Return Aren't Enough as Miami Steals One From CMU, 28-27
articles.byline: Brynn Haverkamp, The Central Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Miami (OH) 28, Central Michigan 27 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Kelly/Shorts Stadium
articles.text:
Hey there, Chippewas. Brynn Haverkamp here, blaze-orange beanie on, and four sack tags filled on the kitchen table. Usually that's a happy week at my house. Saturday at Kelly/Shorts Stadium, Miami beat Central Michigan 28-27, and I'm sitting in the deer stand of sadness.

Here's what happened.

First, the big hunt. Early in the third, Justin Taylor intercepted Caleb Heavner and returned it 46 yards for a touchdown. Seventeen to 14, Chips. Ope, interception! Then, late in the third, Jadyn Glasser hit Langston Lewis for a 9-yard touchdown, and with 4:17 left, Caden VanHuis kicked a 22-yard field goal. Central Michigan 27, Miami 21. I started loading the snowmobile for a victory lap.

Second, the miss. Miami drove 75 yards in eight plays. We were flagged for pass interference twice in a row near the goal line, and D'Shawntae Jones scored from the 2 with 1:41 left. Twenty-eight to 27. Ope.

Third, the last chance. A holding penalty wiped out Glasser's 21-yard run, and our fourth-down pass fell incomplete with 53 seconds left. Season's over on that trail.

My hero is Langston Lewis: 10 catches for 163 yards and a touchdown, including a 47-yarder. Justin Taylor scored on the interception return, and Brett McCalla had another interception. Our defense filled four sack tags, with JJ Douglas, Antonio Cherry Jr. and Nathan VanTimmeren each getting one. Glasser threw for 221 yards without a turnover.

My affectionate goat: the penalty flags. Ten of them for 83 yards, including two on the winning drive. You can't shoot before legal hunting hours, fellas.

What it means: Central Michigan is 3-5 and 1-3 in the MAC after three straight losses, two of them by a touchdown or less. That stings. But Mount Pleasant struck oil in 1928, so this town knows good things are buried underneath.

Next up, Central Michigan faces Eastern Michigan at Ford Field on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. Ope, sack. Fire up, Chips.

Langston Lewis caught 10 passes for 163 yards and a touchdown.

articles.title: Too Many Shots on Goal: Messiah Burch Runs for 184 and Three Scores, and Bowling Green Falls at Buffalo, 31-24
articles.byline: Darcy Fenwick, The Bowling Green Fanatic
articles.matchup: Buffalo 31, Bowling Green 24 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Broadview Stadium
articles.text:
Darcy Fenwick here, former club goalie, and the only person in Wood County who grades run defense by how many times I yelled "Skate back!" at the TV. On Saturday at Broadview Stadium, Buffalo beat Bowling Green 31-24. I yelled a lot.

Honestly, our net-minding was fine through the air. Jason Wright threw 21 passes and only completed 13, so that's eight saves. The problem is that Buffalo didn't need to shoot. They skated it straight in.

Here's the game tape.

The good period: Jay Kastantin threw three touchdown passes, including an 18-yarder to Isaiah Dawson, a 40-yarder to Trey Johnson and a 13-yarder to Nakai Amachree. We led 14-7 and 21-14. Myles Bradley sacked Wright and forced a fumble that E. George recovered. That's a big glove save.

The breakaway: tied 21-21, Buffalo kicked a field goal on the first play of the fourth. Then Messiah Burch broke a 73-yard touchdown run. Thirty-one to 21. That's a breakaway, folks, and nobody was back.

The pulled goalie: Kastantin threw an interception on the next drive, but Buffalo missed a 47-yard field goal. We drove for a Travis Kenner field goal, and then our defense stopped Buffalo on downs at our 38 with 1:02 left. We got to the Buffalo 39 when time ran out. So close. That's hitting the post at the buzzer.

My hero is Kastantin: 19 of 27 for 217 yards and three touchdowns. Our offense also held the ball for almost 36 minutes.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. Burch ran 33 times for 184 yards, and Buffalo ran for 251. You can't stop pucks you never see coming.

What it means: Bowling Green is 2-6 and 2-2 in the MAC, after two losses in a row by a combined eight points. Bowling Green sits on land that used to be the Great Black Swamp, and right now, this season feels pretty swampy. But we drained that swamp once. We'll do it again.

Next up, Bowling Green visits Western Michigan at Waldo Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on CBSSN. Halloween at Waldo. Wear a mask, and maybe a cup. Lace 'em up, Falcons.

articles.title: Forecast: Heavy Burch With a Chance of Glory, as Messiah Burch Runs for a Career-High 184 Yards and Buffalo Beats BG, 31-24
articles.byline: Kendra Woolcott, The Buffalo Fanatic
articles.matchup: Buffalo 31, Bowling Green 24 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Broadview Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, Western New York. Kendra Woolcott with your Bulls weather report. Current conditions: 5-3, 3-1 in the MAC, three straight wins, and a warm front parked over Broadview Stadium. On Saturday, Buffalo beat Bowling Green 31-24. Today's forecast: smiles, with scattered high-fives.

Here's the radar.

Morning showers: Bowling Green's Jay Kastantin threw three touchdown passes, and we trailed 14-7 and 21-14. I had the umbrella out. But Jason Wright ran 39 yards to set up his own 14-yard touchdown pass to Clint Walker just before halftime, and Messiah Burch's 2-yard run tied it at 21 in the third.

Afternoon clearing: Oliver Hautanen kicked a 31-yard field goal on the first play of the fourth quarter. Then, at 12:18, Burch broke through the middle and ran 73 yards for a touchdown. Thirty-one to 21. That's what meteorologists call a high-pressure system.

Evening calm: Miles Greer intercepted Kastantin at the BG 40 on the next drive. Sedrick Vessah had another interception in the third quarter. Bowling Green kicked a late field goal, and our final drive was stopped on downs, but they ran out of time at our 39.

My hero is Messiah Burch, who ran 33 times for a career-high 184 yards and three touchdowns. Will Clark had a sack and a half, too.

And get this: Buffalo had zero penalties. None. Not one flag all afternoon. That's a clear sky, folks.

My affectionate goat: the end of the game. Up a touchdown with about two minutes left, we didn't get the first down, and Bowling Green got the ball back. A little late-day turbulence. Next time, let's land the plane.

What it means: Buffalo is 5-3 and 3-1 in the MAC, part of a three-way tie for second, one game behind Ohio. Buffalo was the end of the Erie Canal in 1825. This team keeps going farther than that.

Next up, Buffalo visits Miami at Yager Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 7 p.m. ET. A November night in Oxford. Stay warm, Bulls fans. Bring a thermos, bring a friend, bring the whole family, and bring your loudest voice, because this team has earned a crowd that sounds like it believes.

articles.title: Worth Setting the Alarm For: Micah Alejado Throws Three Touchdowns, DeVon Rice Runs for Three, and Hawai'i Rolls in DeKalb, 56-21
articles.byline: Kainoa Akana-Baird, The Hawai'i Fanatic
articles.matchup: Hawai'i 56, Northern Illinois 21 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Huskie Stadium
articles.text:
Aloha kakou. Kainoa Akana-Baird here, on the lanai with a plate lunch and a whiteboard full of time-zone math. Saturday's kickoff in DeKalb was 9:30 a.m. in Honolulu. By the time I'd finished my second cup of coffee, Hawai'i had beaten Northern Illinois 56-21. Best breakfast of the year.

Here's how the morning went.

First, the swell builds. The game was tied 14-14 early in the second quarter. Then DeVon Rice broke a 33-yard touchdown run, and the waves started rolling. Micah Alejado hit Cam Barfield on a 62-yard catch-and-run to the NIU 3, and Barfield punched it in from the 1 soon after. After Jeremiah Hughes intercepted Taron Dickens, Alejado found Audric Harris for 44 yards and then Frank Abreu for a 12-yard touchdown with 23 seconds left in the half. Thirty-five to 14.

Second, the wave doesn't stop. Elijah Palmer recovered a fumble early in the third, and Rice scored again from the 5. Then Alejado hit Josiah Fetui for a 44-yard touchdown. That made it 35 straight points. Shaka, brah.

Third, the clean finish. Kydel Stone intercepted Dickens late, and TJ Fo'ilefutu added a 6-yard touchdown. Northern Illinois turned it over five times.

My hero is Micah Alejado, who threw for 323 yards and three touchdowns. DeVon Rice ran for three scores, and Frank Abreu caught two touchdown passes.

My affectionate goat: Alejado's fourth-quarter interception. Brah, we were up 35. You can take the rest of the morning off.

What it means: Hawai'i is 2-6 and 1-4 in the Mountain West, and it snapped a four-game losing streak. We scored 56 points, which is more than our previous two games combined. Hawai'i is the westernmost state, but on Saturday, the Rainbow Warriors made themselves right at home in the Midwest.

Next up, Hawai'i visits UTEP at the Sun Bowl on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff time and TV are still to be announced, so the whiteboard is ready and the marker is uncapped. Island time, but on schedule.

articles.title: Rough Harvest: DeAree Rogers Catches Two Touchdowns, but Five Turnovers Bury Northern Illinois Against Hawai'i, 56-21
articles.byline: Nola Brandvik, The Northern Illinois Fanatic
articles.matchup: Hawai'i 56, Northern Illinois 21 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Huskie Stadium
articles.text:
Hi there, Huskie fans. Nola Brandvik here, on the tailgate of my pickup outside DeKalb, watching the combines finish the bean fields. Everybody around here is bringing in a crop. On Saturday at Huskie Stadium, Hawai'i harvested ours. The Rainbow Warriors beat Northern Illinois 56-21.

I'm not going to sugarcoat it. Hawai'i flew across an ocean and played like it was a home game.

Here's how it went.

First, the good seed. Taron Dickens hit DeAree Rogers for a 49-yard touchdown in the first quarter and a 25-yard touchdown early in the second. Fourteen to 14. I said, "Maybe this is the year." I always say that in October.

Second, the hailstorm. Hawai'i scored the next 35 points. DeVon Rice ran 33 yards for a touchdown. Cam Barfield took a short pass 62 yards. Then Jeremiah Hughes intercepted Dickens late in the half, and Hawai'i scored again with 23 seconds left. By halftime, it was 35-14. Early in the third, Telly Johnson Jr. fumbled after a 12-yard run, and Rice scored from the 5.

Third, the stubble. Elijah Porter ran in a 3-yard touchdown in the fourth, and Yassine Falke intercepted Micah Alejado. Good for them. Those are the little things you gather off the field after the combine goes through.

My hero is DeAree Rogers: eight catches, 115 yards and two touchdowns. Dickens threw for 171 yards and two scores, and Johnson ran for 63 yards.

My affectionate goat: ball security. Five turnovers, fellas. Joseph Glidden patented barbed wire here in 1874. Hold on to the ball like you're holding barbed wire... wait, no. Hold on to it tighter than that.

What it means: Northern Illinois is 0-7 and 0-3 in the Mountain West. It's a rough year in the field. But DeKalb hybrid corn was once planted by more farmers than any other brand, so this town knows how to grow something.

Next up, Northern Illinois visits UNLV at Allegiant Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 10:30 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Halloween in the desert. Lights, costumes and maybe a first win. Knee-high by the Fourth of July. A win by the end of October.

articles.title: Seven-Eight Time in Annapolis: Justin Stevenson Catches 209 Yards, Jahiem White Seals It, and North Texas Outlasts Navy, 49-39
articles.byline: Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, The North Texas Fanatic
articles.matchup: North Texas 49, Navy 39 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Mean Green, baby. Grady Mayhew-Ochoa here, sticks in my back pocket and my heart still doing a drum solo. Saturday at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium, North Texas beat Navy 49-39. That wasn't a football game. That was a 60-minute jam session where both bands refused to stop playing.

Here's the setlist.

Track one, the big hits. Tayven Jackson found Justin Stevenson for a 45-yard touchdown on our first drive and a 53-yarder in the third. Stevenson caught eight passes for 209 yards. That's a solo, baby. Crash cymbal on every catch.

Track two, the special guests. Dalton Carnes returned a punt 76 yards for a touchdown in the second quarter. Then, in the third, Zakye Barker scooped up a Navy fumble and ran 63 yards for another score. When your defense and special teams both take a solo, you know the band is cooking.

Track three, the closer. Navy kept coming, and after Michael Barrow's 4-yard run with 10:49 left, it was 42-39. My hi-hat was shaking. On our very next drive, Jahiem White ran 59 yards to the end zone. Forty-nine to 39. Then we held the ball for the final 6:32 with a 12-play drive. That's a fade-out, baby. The crowd goes home.

My hero is Justin Stevenson, but Jahiem White deserves an encore: 174 rushing yards, two touchdowns and four catches. Jackson threw for 305 yards and three touchdowns on 17-of-23 passing.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. Navy ran 65 times for 363 yards. Jackson Gutierrez alone ran for 228. My drummer brain needs a nap.

What it means: North Texas is 5-2 and 3-0 in the American after four straight wins. Denton's College of Music was the first school to offer a jazz studies degree, and Saturday, this team played like it graduated with honors.

Next up, Florida Atlantic comes to DATCU Stadium on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN. Thursday night, national TV, home crowd. Count it off. Seven-eight time, baby.

articles.title: Logbook Entry: 506 Yards, 228 From Jackson Gutierrez, and a Comeback That Fell Three Points Short as North Texas Beats Navy, 49-39
articles.byline: Cmdr. (Ret.) Annabel Merriweather, The Navy Fanatic
articles.matchup: North Texas 49, Navy 39 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium
articles.text:
Good morning, shipmates. Commander Annabel Merriweather, retired, reporting from the seawall in Annapolis. I've been keeping my logbook for a long time, and I'll record Saturday honestly: North Texas beat Navy 49-39 at Navy-Marine Corps Memorial Stadium. We ran for 363 yards and still lost. The logbook has a few water stains this morning.

Entry one: the leaks. Our defense couldn't stop the deep passes. Justin Stevenson caught 209 yards worth of them. Worse, two special-teams plays sank us. A fumbled snap led to a punt, and Dalton Carnes returned it 76 yards for a touchdown, and Zakye Barker returned a fumble 63 yards for a touchdown in the third.

Entry two: the counterattack. Jackson Gutierrez ran for an 18-yard touchdown, a 1-yarder and a 43-yarder, then threw a two-point conversion pass to Jake Norris. Irabonoise Oniha intercepted Tayven Jackson, and Gutierrez hit Michael Barrow for a 15-yard touchdown pass late in the third. Barrow ran in from the 4 early in the fourth. Forty-two to 39. I was on my feet on the seawall. Full speed ahead.

Entry three: the torpedo. On North Texas' very next drive, Jahiem White ran 59 yards for a touchdown. Then they held the ball for the last 6:32. We never got it back.

My hero is Jackson Gutierrez: 26 carries, 228 yards, three rushing touchdowns and a touchdown pass. Barrow ran for 92 yards and scored twice, and the team committed only one penalty all day. That's a disciplined crew.

My affectionate goat: the deep pass defense, which let Stevenson catch passes of 45, 46 and 53 yards. Fellas, we need more sailors in the deep water.

What it means: Navy is 2-5 and 1-4 in the American, with two straight losses in shootouts. George Washington resigned his commission in Annapolis, but this team doesn't quit.

Next up, Navy plays Notre Dame at Gillette Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at noon ET on ABC. One of college football's oldest series, on Halloween, on national TV. Brace for heavy seas. Steady as she goes.

articles.title: Overcooked in Muncie: Jace Wilson's 65-Yard Score and Boogsie Silvera's Two Interceptions Can't Save the Dish as Ball State Wins, 34-17
articles.byline: Mateo Villaseñor, The Sacramento State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Ball State 34, Sacramento State 17 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Scheumann Stadium
articles.text:
Welcome to the kitchen, Hornets. Mateo Villaseñor here, apron on, smoke alarm going off. On Saturday at Scheumann Stadium, Ball State beat Sacramento State 34-17. We had good ingredients. We left it in the oven a little too long.

Here's tonight's recipe review.

The appetizer was delicious. Grant Meadors kicked a 47-yard field goal, and after Ball State answered, Jackson Sharman threw a 65-yard touchdown pass to Jace Wilson. Ten to 7, Hornets. Chef's kiss.

The main course burned. Less than a minute after Wilson's score, Keldric Luster hit Jamarion McDougle for 55 yards and a touchdown. Then, with 38 seconds left in the half, Sharman was sacked and fumbled at our 26. TJ Horton scored a 1-yard touchdown. Twenty to 10 at halftime. Luster ran for another score early in the third. That's a kitchen fire, chefs.

The dessert was worth saving. Boogsie Silvera intercepted Luster twice. The second came at the goal line late in the third, and he returned it 24 yards. Sharman also threw a 4-yard touchdown pass to Matt Coleman. That's how you save a dish.

My hero is Boogsie Silvera: two interceptions and 11 tackles. Sharman threw for 187 yards and two touchdowns without an interception. Hamish Adams also punted six times for a 45.3-yard average.

My affectionate goat: the run game. We ran 27 times for 54 yards. That's not a recipe, friends. That's a garnish.

What it means: Sacramento State is 1-7 and 0-5 in its first season in the MAC. It's a hard first year in FBS. But Sacramento is America's Farm-to-Fork Capital. We know good food takes time to grow.

Next up, Kent State comes to Hornet Stadium on Friday, Oct. 30, at 10:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. Friday night lights, home cooking and a national TV audience. Preheat the oven. Plate it up, Hornets.

articles.title: Four Punts, Four Dad Jokes, One Big Win: Keldric Luster Accounts for Three Touchdowns as Ball State Beats Sac State, 34-17
articles.byline: Gus Ponder, The Ball State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Ball State 34, Sacramento State 17 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Scheumann Stadium
articles.text:
Gus Ponder here, coming to you from the garage, where the whiteboard is full of arrows and the punt chart says four. On Saturday at Scheumann Stadium, Ball State beat Sacramento State 34-17. That's two wins in a row, folks. I'm so happy I alphabetized my socket set.

Rules are rules, though. Four punts, four dad jokes. Here we go.

Joke one: Why did the Cardinal sit in the garage? He was waiting for a big play. Well, he didn't have to wait long. Down 3-0 in the second, Keldric Luster threw a 65-yard touchdown pass to Isaiah Thacker.

Joke two: What do you call a bird that won't give up? A comeback Cardinal. Sac State answered with a 65-yard touchdown pass, and less than a minute later, Luster found Jamarion McDougle for 55 yards and a score. Thirteen to 10. Yes, we missed the extra point. I'm not ready to talk about it.

Joke three: Why was the quarterback so calm? Because he had his sacks in order. With 38 seconds left in the half, Kaleb Stewart sacked Jackson Sharman and forced a fumble, and B. Marsh recovered. TJ Horton scored from the 1. Twenty to 10.

Joke four: How does Garfield like his football? Lasagna-style, in layers. Luster ran in from the 6 early in the third, and Horton added a 6-yard touchdown run in the fourth. Thirty-four to 17. Jim Davis studied at Ball State, by the way. I tell everyone.

My hero is Keldric Luster: two touchdown passes, a rushing touchdown and 234 passing yards. Jalen Bonds ran for 77 yards, and Cole Stumbaugh averaged 51.8 yards on his four punts, with a long of 70.

My affectionate goat: interceptions. Luster threw two, and both went to Boogsie Silvera. Keldric, buddy, he's not on our team.

What it means: Ball State is 3-5 and 2-2 in the MAC. The Ball brothers built a glass factory here in 1888, and this season, things are starting to look clearer.

Next up, Ball State visits UMass at Warren McGuirk Alumni Stadium on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. Here's the garage plan:

1. Run the ball. Then run it again. 2. Clean tackling. 3. Keep Stumbaugh rested. Fewer punts, fewer jokes. I'll make that sacrifice.

articles.title: Thirteen Seconds of Heartbreak: A 98-Yard Drive Puts EMU Ahead, a 100-Yard Kickoff Return Takes It Away, and Ohio Wins, 24-20
articles.byline: Imogen Tremblay, The Eastern Michigan Fanatic
articles.matchup: Ohio 24, Eastern Michigan 20 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Peden Stadium
articles.text:
Hi, everybody. Imogen Tremblay here, at my corner table in Depot Town, with a coffee that went cold around 3:53 left in the fourth quarter. On Saturday at Peden Stadium, Ohio beat Eastern Michigan 24-20. We led at halftime, and we led with 3:40 left. Then we didn't.

Here's how it went.

First, the scrappy start. Ohio scored first on a 78-yard pass. Then Aaron Kearse scooped up a fumble and ran 25 yards for a touchdown. Quincy Byas recovered a muffed punt, and Rudy Kessinger kicked field goals of 31 and 41 yards, the second as time expired in the half. Thirteen to 10, Eagles.

Second, the drive of the year. Down 17-13 in the fourth, we started at our own 2. Brogan McCaughey hit Tanner Lemaster for 34 yards, and eight plays and 98 yards later, he hit Joey Mattord for a 24-yard touchdown. Twenty to 17 with 3:53 left. I screamed in a coffee shop. Depot Town will recover.

Third, the 13 seconds. On the kickoff, Darren James-Hamilton returned it 100 yards for a touchdown. Our final drive went 13 plays to the Ohio 16, and the last pass fell incomplete at the goal line with five seconds left.

My hero is Joey Mattord, with seven catches, a touchdown and 24 rushing yards. McCaughey completed 27 of 39 passes, Kessinger made both field goals, and Bryce Llewellyn had 11 tackles. And our defense held Ohio to 90 rushing yards.

My affectionate goat: kickoff coverage, obviously. Also third downs: we converted only two of 15. Fellas, that's not how we do it on the gray turf.

What it means: Eastern Michigan is 4-5 and 3-2 in the MAC. Ypsilanti built more than 8,500 B-24 bombers at Willow Run, so this town knows how to rebuild things fast.

Next up, Eastern Michigan faces Central Michigan at Ford Field on Wednesday, Nov. 4. Kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. Michigan rivals, an NFL stadium and our pride at stake. Gray turf, bright future.

articles.title: Brick by Brick, Then 100 Yards at Once: Darren James-Hamilton's Kickoff Return Lifts Ohio Over Eastern Michigan, 24-20
articles.byline: Penny Trautman, The Ohio Fanatic
articles.matchup: Ohio 24, Eastern Michigan 20 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Peden Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hello from Court Street! Penny Trautman here, standing on the bricks and shaking a little. On Saturday at Peden Stadium, Ohio beat Eastern Michigan 24-20, and the Bobcats are 4-0 in the MAC. I usually build my wins one brick at a time. Saturday, Darren James-Hamilton laid 100 yards of them in 13 seconds.

Here's how we built it.

The first brick: Nick Poulos hit Dom Dorwart for a 78-yard touchdown in the first quarter. Dorwart caught four passes for 125 yards. That's a load-bearing wall.

The wobbly bricks: Eastern Michigan returned a fumble for a touchdown, and James-Hamilton fumbled a punt return. We trailed 13-10 at halftime. Poulos ran in from the 1 late in the third to put us ahead 17-13, but the Eagles drove 98 yards for a 20-17 lead with 3:53 left.

The keystone: James-Hamilton took the next kickoff at the goal line and ran 100 yards for a touchdown. Earlier, he also intercepted a pass. Then our defense took over. Eastern Michigan drove to our 4, Michael Molnar forced an intentional grounding penalty that pushed it back to our 16, and the final throw fell incomplete with five seconds left. Mortar set!

My hero is Darren James-Hamilton: an interception, a fumble and a 100-yard kickoff return touchdown. That's a whole season of emotions in one game. Molnar made 18 tackles and had a sack, and Jack Fries had two sacks.

My affectionate goat: third downs. We converted three of 11. And our run game only got 90 yards. Bricks are supposed to be heavy, fellas. Put some weight behind it.

What it means: Ohio is 6-2 and 4-0 in the MAC after five straight wins, alone at the top of the standings. Peden Stadium has been our home since 1929, and it hasn't seen many finishes better than that one.

Next up, Ohio visits Akron at InfoCision Stadium on Tuesday, Nov. 3, at 7 p.m. ET. Tuesday night MACtion. Brick by brick, Bobcats.

articles.title: Counter: 1,000! ULM Scores 18 Points in the Final 2:34, Billy Pullen Scores on the Last Play, and the Warhawks Get Their First Win at Troy, 21-14
articles.byline: Darnell Vidrine, The UL Monroe Fanatic
articles.matchup: UL Monroe 21, Troy 14 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL)
articles.text:
Good evening, night owls, and welcome back to the overnight show. Darnell Vidrine here, and friends, I need you to turn the radio up. On Saturday at Veterans Memorial Stadium, UL Monroe beat Troy 21-14. That's our first win of the season. The optimism counter just broke. It's at 1,000. I might need a new counter.

Here's how it went down.

For most of the night, it looked like another reset. Troy led 7-3 at halftime and 14-3 after Gavin Griffin's 1-yard touchdown with 6:16 left. But DJ Jester intercepted a pass in the end zone in the second quarter, right after Troy recovered our muffed punt at our 21. Hope was still on the air.

First hit: Aidan Armenta threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to Bryce Anderson with 2:34 left. Fourteen to 9. Our defense forced a three-and-out, and James Smith sacked Tucker Kilcrease. A holding penalty put us at our 14 with 1:40 left.

Second hit: 86 yards in six plays. Zach Palmer-Smith ran 14 yards, and a Troy personal foul added 15 more. Armenta hit P. Fulghum for 19 yards, then Darrion Gilliam for a 16-yard touchdown with 15 seconds left. Fifteen to 14!

Third hit: on the final play, the ball came loose, and Billy Pullen fell on it in the end zone. Twenty-one to 14. Friends, I spilled my coffee on the soundboard. Worth it.

My hero is Aidan Armenta: 13 of 22 for 147 yards and two late touchdowns. Billy Pullen had the winning touchdown, Kevontay Wells had a sack and a half, and Noah Flemmings had 15 tackles. Our defense held Troy to 47 passing yards.

My affectionate goat: two failed two-point tries. They made my heart skip beats. Our hearts are fine now. Mostly.

What it means: UL Monroe is 1-6 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt. Monroe is where the crop-dusting company that became Delta got started. Tonight, the Warhawks took off.

Next up, Southern Miss comes to Malone Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home. Counter: reset to 100. Keep the faith, Warhawks.

articles.title: Upside Down and Inside Out: Troy Leads 14-3 With 6:16 Left, Then Gives Up 18 Points as ULM Steals One, 21-14
articles.byline: Marlo Pickens, The Troy Fanatic
articles.matchup: UL Monroe 21, Troy 14 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Veterans Memorial Stadium (AL)
articles.text:
Hey there, buddy. Marlo Pickens, former Trojan long snapper, peanut farmer's son, and a man staring at the world upside down. On Saturday at Veterans Memorial Stadium, UL Monroe beat Troy 21-14. I flipped that game over every way I know, and it still looks bad. ULM hadn't won a game all year.

Here's the row-by-row count.

The planting: our defense was stout for 57 minutes. Gavin Griffin caught a 5-yard touchdown pass from Tucker Kilcrease in the first quarter and ran in from the 1 with 6:16 left. Fourteen to 3. I started counting my peanuts before they were boiled.

The weeds: Aidan Armenta threw a 12-yard touchdown with 2:34 left. We went three-and-out, and Kilcrease got sacked. Then, with 1:40 left, ULM drove 86 yards, helped by our 15-yard personal foul, and Armenta threw a 16-yard touchdown with 15 seconds left. Fifteen to 14.

The hailstorm: on the final play, we fumbled, and Billy Pullen fell on it in the end zone. Twenty-one to 14. I sat on the tailgate for an hour.

Earlier, we wasted a gift. We recovered a muffed punt at the ULM 21 in the second quarter, and moments later, our pass was intercepted in the end zone. That's a whole row of peanuts left in the field.

My hero is Jordan Lovett, who ran 17 times for 70 yards. Keno Jones had 12 tackles, and Ty Clemons and Donnie Smith had sacks.

My affectionate goat: the passing game. Forty-seven yards, fellas. I've thrown farther than that... well, backwards, between my legs.

What it means: Troy is 3-4 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt, with its first home loss of the season. Troy used to be called Deer Stand Hill, and right now, we're sitting in that deer stand waiting for something good to walk by.

Next up, Troy visits James Madison at Bridgeforth Stadium on Thursday, Oct. 29, at 7:30 p.m. ET on ESPN2. A short week, a tough road trip and a national TV crowd. Come early, buddy. Bring a sack of boiled peanuts. Bring two. I'll bring the puns.

articles.title: The Ledger Doesn't Balance: Lunch Winfield Throws for 299, but Jamarice Wilder's Late Touchdown Sends Louisiana Home Short, 35-31
articles.byline: Amélie 'Mimi' Fontenot, The Louisiana Fanatic
articles.matchup: Southern Miss 35, Louisiana 31 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Renasant Stadium
articles.text:
Allons danser, mes amis... slowly, tonight. Mimi Fontenot here, ledger open, accordion on low. On Saturday in Hattiesburg, Southern Miss beat Louisiana 35-31. I've audited this one three times. The numbers are correct, and I don't like them.

Here's the accounting.

Credits: Lunch Winfield ran for a touchdown, threw a 4-yard touchdown to Trenton Chaney with 31 seconds left in the first half and then threw a 31-yard touchdown pass to Anthony Reagan Jr. late in the third. JJ Garner broke a 42-yard touchdown run. We led 28-21 going into the fourth. That was a beautiful two-step.

Debits: early in the fourth, Kolby Peavy intercepted Winfield and scored. Twenty-eight to 28. A double-entry error if I've ever seen one.

The final balance: Tony Sterner kicked a 22-yard field goal with 2:51 left. Thirty-one to 28, Cajuns. But Southern Miss drove 75 yards in eight plays. Jamarice Wilder ran 28 yards and then 16 yards for the winning touchdown with 58 seconds left. We got a nice kickoff return to midfield, but after one short completion, three straight passes fell incomplete. The dance floor went dark.

My hero is Lunch Winfield: 299 passing yards, two touchdown passes and a rushing touchdown. Jake St. Andre had 11 tackles and a sack, and Maxie Baudoin IV added another sack. Our offense held the ball for over 34 minutes.

My affectionate goat: the run defense. Southern Miss ran for 286 yards, and Steven Robinson scored three times. Also fourth downs: we went zero for three. That's a write-off.

What it means: Louisiana is 5-3 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt. Lafayette is the Heart of Acadiana, and hearts can take a hit. Ours will start dancing again soon.

Next up, South Alabama comes to Our Lady of Lourdes Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7. Kickoff time and TV are still to be announced. That gives us an open week to rest up, rebalance the books and polish the two-step shoes. Laissez les bons stats rouler!

articles.title: Sweet Tea and Sweeter Finishes: Steven Robinson Scores Three Times, Jamarice Wilder Wins It Late, and Southern Miss Tops Louisiana, 35-31
articles.byline: Delphine 'Dee' Broussard, The Southern Miss Fanatic
articles.matchup: Southern Miss 35, Louisiana 31 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Renasant Stadium
articles.text:
Well, hey there, sugar. Dee Broussard, on my porch in the Pine Belt, and this week, my sweet tea and my disposition are equally sweet. On Saturday in Hattiesburg, Southern Miss beat Louisiana 35-31. That's our first win since the season opener, sugar, and it was worth every gray hair.

Here's the tea.

Pour one: Steven Robinson ran for three touchdowns in the first half, from 8, 4 and 10 yards. He carried 22 times for 145 yards. Bless that young man's legs.

Pour two: we trailed 28-21 heading into the fourth. Then Kolby Peavy intercepted Lunch Winfield and scored. Tied, 28-28. I spilled my tea all over my bow. Worth it.

Pour three: Louisiana kicked a field goal with 2:51 left to take a 31-28 lead. Our offense drove 75 yards in eight plays, and Jamarice Wilder ran 28 yards and then 16 yards for the touchdown with 58 seconds left. Then our defense forced three straight incompletions, and Landry Lyddy took a knee. Sugar, I hugged a stranger.

My hero is Jamarice Wilder: 13 carries, 154 yards and the winning touchdown. Robinson ran for three scores, and we ran for 286 yards as a team. Michael Robinson III had 12 tackles and a sack.

My affectionate goat: the kicking game. Creighton Wilbanks missed his only field goal try, a 41-yarder. Also, our fourth-down offense went four for seven, with three stops. Sometimes a lady has to punt, sugar.

What it means: Southern Miss is 2-5 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt, and that ended a five-game losing streak. The Golden Eagles won conference titles in 1996, 1997, 1999, 2006 and 2011. We're not there yet, but Saturday felt like the start.

Next up, Southern Miss visits UL Monroe at Malone Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on ESPN+. A Halloween road trip, a fresh win and a new bow. To the top, sugar. We're just climbing from the bottom step.

articles.title: The Court Is Not Amused: Old Dominion Is Held to Minus-13 Rushing Yards in a 26-0 Loss at Louisiana Tech
articles.byline: Winifred 'Winnie' Pocklington, The Old Dominion Fanatic
articles.matchup: Louisiana Tech 26, Old Dominion 0 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Joe Aillet Stadium
articles.text:
Hear ye, hear ye! The royal court of Old Dominion is now in session, and I'm sorry to report that the crown is crooked for a reason. Winnie Pocklington presiding. On Saturday at Joe Aillet Stadium, Louisiana Tech beat Old Dominion 26-0. We didn't score a single point. The royal scribe has nothing to write.

Here's the court record.

Exhibit A: the slow start. Louisiana Tech scored two touchdowns in the first quarter. Blake Baker ran in from the 4, and Trey Kukuk ran in from the 5. Fourteen to zero in the first quarter.

Exhibit B: the missed chance. Our defense did hold firm at the goal line before halftime, stopping Louisiana Tech on downs at our 10. Then, in the third quarter, we drove for a 40-yard field goal, and Nathanial Eichner missed. That would've been our only points, your honor.

Exhibit C: the lockdown. Louisiana Tech's defense sacked Jaxon Potter six times, and we ran for minus-13 yards on 22 carries. Amari Butler intercepted Potter in the fourth quarter. The castle walls held for them, not us.

My hero is Ja'Mez Drummer: 15 tackles. Koa Naotala had two sacks, and DeAndre Lynch had another. Our defense kept it to 26, which is something. Leon Haughton Jr. and Josh Rodriguez caught four passes each.

My affectionate goat: the running game. Negative 13 yards. In Norfolk, we have the world's largest naval base. On Saturday, we couldn't find a little room to run.

What it means: Old Dominion is 2-6 and 1-4 in the Sun Belt. It's a hard year at court. But this program went 9-2 in its first season back in 2009. Monarchs always reclaim the throne.

Next up, Marshall comes to S.B. Ballard Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 1 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home. Bring your crown, your cape and your loudest voice. Long live the Monarchs. Hear ye, hear ye: the court is adjourned.

articles.title: Two Shutouts, One Orchard: Blake Baker Completes 28 of 34, the Defense Sacks ODU Six Times, and Louisiana Tech Wins 26-0
articles.byline: Booker 'Champ' Tullos, The Louisiana Tech Fanatic
articles.matchup: Louisiana Tech 26, Old Dominion 0 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Joe Aillet Stadium
articles.text:
Well, howdy, and welcome to the orchard. Champ Tullos here, former fullback and full-time peach man. On Saturday at Joe Aillet Stadium, Louisiana Tech beat Old Dominion 26-0. That's two straight shutouts, folks. Our defense hasn't allowed a point in eight quarters. These peaches are ripe.

Here's how we picked the crop. Well, harvested it. You know what I mean.

First, the fast start. We scored two touchdowns in the first quarter. Blake Baker ran in from the 4, and Trey Kukuk ran in from the 5. That's my kind of football, right up the middle, fullback style.

Second, the air show. Baker completed 28 of 34 passes for 303 yards. Eli Finley caught 10 passes for 128 yards, including a 2-yard touchdown in the third quarter. Jalen Mickens caught eight for 110, including a 36-yarder to set up a Hunter Rioux 49-yard field goal.

Third, the brick wall. Our defense sacked Jaxon Potter six times. Jadon Mayfield had two, and Alonzo Jackson Jr. and Justice Williams had one and a half each. Old Dominion ran for minus-13 yards. Amari Butler intercepted Potter in the fourth quarter, and we stopped them on fourth down twice.

My hero is the whole defense, but Jadon Mayfield gets the first peach. Baker gets the second, for throwing and running for touchdowns. And Kaegan Kent added a 25-yard field goal.

My affectionate goat: penalties. Nine for 75 yards. And we got stuffed on a fourth down at the 10 before halftime. A fullback would've scored there, I'm just saying.

What it means: Louisiana Tech is 5-2 and 3-0 in the Sun Belt, in our first year in the league. We've played football since 1901, and Saturday felt like one of the good ones. Ruston has a Peach Festival every June, but we're celebrating early this year.

Next up, Louisiana Tech visits South Alabama at Hancock Whitney Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+. A Halloween trip to Mobile. Come early, bring a lawn chair, and if anybody offers you a peach, say yes ma'am.

articles.title: Release Notes: Third Downs Broken, Kickoff Coverage Broken, and San José State Falls at Nevada, 28-13
articles.byline: Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, The San José State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Nevada 28, San José State 13 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Mackay Stadium
articles.text:
Hey, team. Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz here, at my standing desk in downtown San Jose, staring at a whiteboard full of red tickets. On Saturday at Mackay Stadium, Nevada beat San José State 28-13. This release did not pass QA.

Here's the retro.

Bug one: third downs. We converted one of 14. One! Nevada held the ball for more than 38 minutes, and our offense managed 204 yards. That's a blocker, team. Priority zero.

Bug two: the trick play. Down 14-3 early in the fourth, Nevada's Marshaun Brown, who'd already caught a touchdown pass, threw a 32-yard touchdown to Herschel Turner. Twenty-one to 3. Nobody had that one in the spec.

Bug three: kickoff coverage. Luke Weaver hit Dominique McKenzie for 47 yards, and Viliami Teu ran in an 11-yard touchdown. Twenty-one to 10, and we had a little momentum. Then K. Woods returned the kickoff 90 yards to our 8, and Nevada scored on the next play. That's what we call a regression.

What shipped: Trajan Sinatra made field goals of 38 and 41 yards. Jayden Robertson intercepted a pass, and Solomone Langi and Etu Finau had sacks. Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa made 12 tackles, and Naseri Danielson made 11. Our offense also didn't turn it over.

My hero is Tuli Tagovailoa-Amosa, who also stopped Nevada on fourth down near midfield before halftime. Viliami Teu ran for our touchdown.

My affectionate goat: the penalty flags. Eight for 74 yards. Team, please stop filing bugs against yourselves.

What it means: San José State is 4-4 and 2-2 in the Mountain West. Our sprint velocity is down, but the roadmap still works. San Jose was California's first state capital. We know how to get things started.

Next up, New Mexico comes to CEFCU Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 4 p.m. ET on MW+. Halloween at home: costume optional, loud required. Ship it to prod.

articles.title: Happy 130th, Pack: Luke Duncan Throws Two Touchdowns, Marshaun Brown Throws One, and Nevada Beats San José State on Its Birthday, 28-13
articles.byline: Ridge Corbell, The Nevada Fanatic
articles.matchup: Nevada 28, San José State 13 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Mackay Stadium
articles.text:
Yo, Pack nation. Ridge Corbell here, on the tailgate of my truck outside Reno, board waxed and birthday cake in the cooler. On Saturday, Nevada football turned 130, and the Wolf Pack celebrated at Mackay Stadium by beating San José State 28-13. Fresh powder, baby. Nobody lost at their own party.

Here's the run, top to bottom.

The first turn: Luke Duncan hit Marshaun Brown for a 4-yard touchdown in the first quarter. Then Duncan threw a 25-yard touchdown pass to Trace Estes in the third. Fourteen to 3.

The trick: early in the fourth, Brown flipped the script and threw a 32-yard touchdown pass to Herschel Turner. A receiver touchdown pass on your 130th birthday? That's a backflip off the big kicker, dude.

The landing: SJSU scored to make it 21-10. Then K. Woods took the kickoff 90 yards to the SJSU 8, and after a penalty, Dominic Kelley ran in from the 4 on the next play. Twenty-eight to 10. Send it.

My hero is Marshaun Brown, with a touchdown catch, a touchdown pass and five catches. Duncan completed 18 of 29 for 178 yards and two scores. Kelley ran 24 times for 82 yards. Dylan LaBarbera had two sacks, and our defense held San José State to one third-down conversion in 14 tries. We also held the ball for over 38 minutes.

My affectionate goat: the second-quarter pass by Reeve Slone that got intercepted. Not every backflip lands, bro.

What it means: Nevada is 3-4 and 2-2 in the Mountain West. Mackay Stadium's field is at 4,610 feet, and on Saturday, the Pack were flying even higher than that.

Next up, Nevada visits UCLA at the Rose Bowl on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 4:15 p.m. ET on BTN. A Halloween trip to Pasadena, a big stage and a chance at a big run. Light the candles. Send it.

articles.title: Painted Blue in the Fourth: Dylan Riley Runs for 128 Yards and Two Late Touchdowns as Boise State Pulls Away at Washington State, 31-10
articles.byline: Thatcher Bluestem, The Boise State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Boise State 31, Washington State 10 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Gesa Field at Martin Stadium
articles.text:
Morning, Bronco Nation. Thatcher Bluestem here, on my back porch in the North End with my coffee and Turf the heeler, who I'm telling you is blue in spirit. On Saturday at Martin Stadium, Boise State beat Washington State 31-10. For three quarters, it was gray. In the fourth, we painted it blue.

articles.title: Three Good Quarters on the Palouse: Washington State Ties Boise State 10-10, Then the Broncos Pull Away, 31-10
articles.byline: Hank Palouse, The Washington State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Boise State 31, Washington State 10 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Gesa Field at Martin Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy, Cougs. Hank Palouse here, in the cab of my pickup outside town, looking out at the wheat stubble. On Saturday at Martin Stadium, Boise State beat Washington State 31-10. I'll be honest with you: for three quarters, we went toe to toe with a ranked team. Then the fourth quarter showed up like a combine.

Here's the harvest report.

The good soil: Kirby Vorhees ran in a 1-yard touchdown just before halftime to tie it 7-7. Jack Stevens booted a 47-yard field goal in the third, and it was 10-10 entering the fourth quarter. I honked my horn. The cows looked at me funny.

The hailstorm: early in the fourth, Boise State scored on a 6-yard pass. On our next drive, Boen Phelps intercepted Owen Eshelman and set up a 33-yard touchdown run by Dylan Riley. Then Riley broke a 72-yard touchdown run from his own 10. Twenty-one points in about seven minutes.

The last row: we drove 13 plays, 72 yards to the Boise goal line. On fourth down, Eshelman's pass to Branden Ganashamoorthy was broken up at the goal line. So close, Cougs.

My hero is Owen Eshelman, who threw for 191 yards and ran 23 times. He took some hits and kept getting up. Ganashamoorthy caught four passes for 58 yards, Keith Brown had nine tackles, and we converted four of five fourth downs.

My affectionate goat: the run game. We ran 33 times for 53 yards. That's less than two yards a carry, fellas. Lentils grow faster.

What it means: Washington State is 1-7 and 0-4 in the Pac-12. That's a tough season to look at. But Ol' Crimson has flown at every College GameDay since 2003, and we Cougs don't stop waving.

Next up, Washington State visits San Diego State at Snapdragon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7 p.m. ET on CBSSN. A Halloween road trip to sunshine country. I know the record. I know who's coming. I'm waving it anyway.

articles.title: Big Waves, Wipeout Ending: Stone Saunders Throws for 369 Yards, but San Diego State Falls at Colorado State, 56-49
articles.byline: Kai Delgado-Sorensen, The San Diego State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Colorado State 56, San Diego State 49 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Canvas Stadium
articles.text:
What's up from Pacific Beach, Aztec nation. Kai Delgado-Sorensen here, wetsuit peeled down, fish taco half-eaten, still processing. On Saturday at Canvas Stadium, Colorado State beat San Diego State 56-49. Dude. That was a 105-point swell. We rode a lot of waves. We just wiped out on a few too many.

Here's the surf report.

Set one: Stone Saunders was carving. He threw for 369 yards, and Jaylon Hawkins caught six passes for 164, including a 43-yard touchdown. Javion Kinnard ran for touchdowns of 19 and 32 yards. It was 24-21 us in the second quarter. Glassy conditions, bro.

Set two: then the closeout. Colorado State scored twice late in the half, and the second one was a 38-yard interception return by Tre'Shawn Moore. Thirty-five to 24 at halftime. That's getting caught inside, dude.

Set three: the comeback swell. Down 56-42, Saunders threw an interception that D'Mon Brinson returned to our 3. But on the very next play, G. Lightfoot forced and recovered a Hauss Hejny fumble at our 1. Then our offense went 99 yards in 16 plays, and Lucky Sutton ran in from the 7 with 1:57 left. Fifty-six to 49! But Colorado State got the ball back and ran out the clock.

My hero is G. Lightfoot, for that fumble that gave us one last wave. Hawkins was a freak, Sutton ran for two scores, and Saunders also threw a 24-yard touchdown to Jordan Napier and a two-point conversion to Bert Emanuel Jr. Josh Hunter made 13 tackles.

My affectionate goat: the defense. Five hundred forty-nine yards allowed. Fellas, that's not a defense, that's a beach break with no lifeguard.

What it means: San Diego State is 3-5 and 2-2 in the Pac-12. San Diego is the Birthplace of California, and we can still be born again this season.

Next up, Washington State comes to Snapdragon Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 7 p.m. ET on CBSSN. Halloween by the ocean. Costumes encouraged, wetsuits optional. I'll be watching from the beach, then heading in when the sun drops. Gnarly, dude. Go Aztecs.

articles.title: Five-Touchdown Summit: Hauss Hejny Throws Three, Runs for Two, and Colorado State Survives San Diego State, 56-49
articles.byline: Ansel Rimrock, The Colorado State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Colorado State 56, San Diego State 49 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Canvas Stadium
articles.text:
Morning, Rams. Ansel Rimrock here, at the Horsetooth trailhead with my thermos and a green-and-gold beanie, legs still shaking from the hike. On Saturday at Canvas Stadium, Colorado State beat San Diego State 56-49. That's 105 points at altitude. Even the mountain goats needed oxygen.

Here's the trail map.

Switchback one: Hauss Hejny was simply elevated. He threw touchdown passes to Tommy Maher of 9 and 54 yards. Mel Brown returned a kickoff 62 yards to set up a Durell Robinson touchdown. Robinson scored twice on the ground and caught a 28-yard touchdown.

Switchback two: Tre'Shawn Moore, ladies and gentlemen. With 1:33 left in the first half, he intercepted Stone Saunders and returned it 38 yards for a touchdown. Thirty-five to 24 at halftime. I yodeled. Somebody asked me to stop. I did not.

Switchback three: Hejny ran 30 yards for a touchdown to make it 56-42. Then D'Mon Brinson intercepted Saunders and returned it 49 yards to the SDSU 3. Hejny fumbled at the goal line, though, and San Diego State drove 99 yards to make it 56-49 with 1:57 left. Then we got the ball back at their 44, picked up a first down and Hejny took a knee. Summit reached.

My hero is Hauss Hejny: 24 of 31 for 333 yards, three touchdown passes and two rushing touchdowns. Maher caught six for 108. Oumar Diomande made 13 tackles. We converted nine of 12 third downs.

My affectionate goat: the defense. We allowed 565 yards. Mountain air, thick defense? Not Saturday, friends. Let's just say we needed thick skin.

What it means: Colorado State is 3-4 and 1-2 in the Pac-12, and we snapped a four-game losing streak. Fort Collins inspired Main Street, U.S.A., at Disney's parks, and Saturday felt like a ride.

Next up, Colorado State visits Utah State at Maverik Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 3:30 p.m. ET on USA Network. Halloween in Logan. Pack layers. Mountain air, thick skin. That's this week's motto. Go Rams.

articles.title: Missed the Last Train: Qwantavius Wiggins Runs 77 Yards for a Touchdown, but Georgia State Falls at Arkansas State, 38-32
articles.byline: Malik Overstreet, The Georgia State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Arkansas State 38, Georgia State 32 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Centennial Bank Stadium
articles.text:
Next stop, heartbreak. Malik Overstreet here, MARTA card in one pocket, third-down chart in the other, riding the train home from the station of sadness. On Saturday in Jonesboro, Arkansas State beat Georgia State 38-32. We were one drive from making the connection. We missed it.

Here's the route map.

Stop one: Qwantavius Wiggins. He caught a 33-yard touchdown pass from Ayden Pereira with 26 seconds left in the first half to tie it 14-14. Then in the third quarter, right after Arkansas State took the lead, he ran 77 yards for a touchdown. Twenty-one to 21. That's express service.

Stop two: the delay. Arkansas State scored 17 straight points, with two touchdowns and a field goal. Thirty-eight to 21. That's the Downtown Connector at 5:15 on a Friday.

Stop three: the comeback. Pereira threw a 27-yard touchdown to Rodshaun Dorsey and found Derrick Avery Jr. for two. Then Pereira hit Dorsey for 37 yards, and Samer Layous kicked a 33-yard field goal. Thirty-eight to 32 with 4:25 left. We got the ball back at our 13 with 1:49 left and drove into Arkansas State territory. Then Makai Shahid intercepted Pereira at the 6 with 15 seconds left. Doors closing.

My hero is Qwantavius Wiggins: 99 rushing yards, five catches and two touchdowns. Dorsey caught three passes for 85 yards. Cameran Brown threw a touchdown to DJ Riles. Jaydon Hood made 10 tackles, and Tre Mittman and Coby Owens each had sacks.

My affectionate goat: the two interceptions. And three-for-12 on third down. You know I keep the chart, Panthers.

What it means: Georgia State is 4-3 and 1-2 in the Sun Belt. Center Parc Stadium was built for the 1996 Olympics, and we still have time to finish the race.

Next up, Coastal Carolina comes to Center Parc Stadium on Saturday, Oct. 31, at 2 p.m. ET on ESPN+. Halloween at home, Panthers. Take the train. Next stop, Center Parc. Mind the gap, and mind the Chanticleers.

articles.title: Let It Rip: Trey Owens Throws Two Touchdowns, Runs for Two More, and Arkansas State Holds Off Georgia State, 38-32
articles.byline: Ty Doucet-Harmon, The Arkansas State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Arkansas State 38, Georgia State 32 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, Centennial Bank Stadium
articles.text:
Quaaack. Ty Doucet-Harmon here, Delta duck guide and Red Wolves lifer, with my duck call around my neck and my voice mostly gone. On Saturday at Centennial Bank Stadium, Arkansas State beat Georgia State 38-32. It came down to the final seconds, folks. I let it rip.

Here's the hunt.

Setting the decoys: Trey Owens threw a 12-yard touchdown pass to Jaylen Bonelli in the first quarter and ran in a 2-yard score in the second. Then early in the third, Brandon Greil intercepted Ayden Pereira, and on the next play Owens hit Nana Burris for a 54-yard touchdown. Twenty-one to 14.

The flock lands: Georgia State tied it on a 77-yard run. Then Owens hit Bonelli for 35 yards and ran in from the 1. Timothy Carter ran in a 2-yard touchdown to start the fourth, and Owens hit Bonelli for 38 yards to set up Clune Van Andel's 26-yard field goal. Thirty-eight to 21. Quaaack.

The last shot: Georgia State pulled within 38-32 and drove into our territory in the final minute. With 15 seconds left, Makai Shahid intercepted Ayden Pereira at our 6. Shahid had an interception called back by a roughing penalty just one play earlier. Second chance, good shot. Dinner's in the cooler, folks.

My hero is Trey Owens: 21 of 32 for 309 yards, two touchdown passes and two rushing touchdowns. Bonelli caught seven passes for 150, and Burris caught six for 114. Joe Drew made 10 tackles, and Tre Stevens and Shakai Woods had sacks. We didn't turn it over.

My affectionate goat: field goals. Van Andel missed from 44 and 48 yards before hitting from 26. And we went two for 10 on third downs.

What it means: Arkansas State is 4-4 and 2-2 in the Sun Belt. We've been the Red Wolves since 2008, and this pack knows how to hunt.

Next up, UL Monroe comes to Centennial Bank Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, at 3 p.m. ET. TV is still to be announced. That means a week off first to rest the calls. Get in the blind early, keep your voice low until it counts, and when it counts, let it rip. Quaaack.

articles.title: One Scoop Short: Anthony Garcia Throws a Touchdown, Utah State Ties It Late, but Texas State Wins 20-17 on a Field Goal
articles.byline: Hyrum Tolleson, The Utah State Fanatic
articles.matchup: Texas State 20, Utah State 17 (final), Sat. Oct. 24, UFCU Stadium
articles.text:
Howdy, Aggies. Hyrum Tolleson here, in my booth at Aggie Ice Cream with a double scoop melting a little faster than usual. On Saturday in San Marcos, Texas State beat Utah State 20-17. We churned for four quarters, folks, and came up one scoop short.

Here's the batch.

The first pour: Kian Afrookhteh made a 43-yard field goal to put us up 3-0. On the ensuing kickoff, Jaylen Jenkins returned it 100 yards for a touchdown. That's the ice cream hitting the floor before you get your first lick.

The churn: Afrookhteh added field goals of 48 and 27 yards, and we led 9-7 at halftime. But Texas State scored 10 straight to go up 17-9.

The rally: we drove 75 yards in 10 plays, and receiver Anthony Garcia threw a 6-yard touchdown pass to Kaina Watson. Grady Brosterhous hit Javen Jacobs for the two-point conversion. Seventeen to 17 with 8:07 left! Texas State answered with a 37-yard field goal with 1:56 left. We drove 13 plays to their 25, but a delay of game pushed us back, and Afrookhteh's 48-yard try missed as time expired.

My hero is Anthony Garcia: eight catches for 87 yards and a touchdown pass. Our defense held the nation's top offense to 250 yards and sacked Brad Jackson four times, one each from Bronson Olevao Jr., Brevin Hamblin, Asher Cunningham and Tyree Morris.
